body_en: Trump DoJ moves to drop legal challenge to Mary Peltola’s Alaska Senate win | US midterm elections 2026
President had sought to block results if Democrat won race that featured two candidates named Dan Sullivan

In a legal filing on Thursday, the Trump administration asked a federal appeals court to dismiss the lawsuit it filed before the midterm elections seeking to block the certification of the US Senate race in Alaska should Democrat Mary Peltola win.

The legal challenge centered around the presence on the ballot of a second candidate with the same name as the incumbent, Republican senator Dan Sullivan. The Alaska supreme court already ruled that the second Sullivan’s candidacy was legal and that he could be on the ballot.
Senate Republicans rejects war powers bill to halt fighting in Iran

Peltola did win the election, with 50.13% of the vote , giving her more than the combined vote totals of all other candidates, including the incumbent Republican senator, Dan Sullivan, and a second Daniel Sullivan, who was reportedly recruited to enter the race by Democrats to siphon votes away from the sitting senator.

The suit was filed at the direction of Donald Trump saying that a Peltola win should not be certified until an investigation can determine if voters were confused. The administration never explained how such an investigation could take place given the secrecy of the ballot.
The administration moved on Thursday to have an appeals court declare its case moot, two days after the race was decided.
Peltola faced significant controversy on the campaign trail, after the New York Times reported that her staffers were involved in a scheme to recruit the “decoy” Dan Sullivan.
Peltola denied any involvement in encouraging the second Sullivan’s run.
Peltola, who is Yup’ik, will join the Minnesota senator-elect Peggy Flanagan, a member of the White Earth band of Ojibwe, as the first two Native American women to serve in the US Senate.

The legal filing came a day after Alaska concluded its vote-count and used ranked-choice tabulation to decide races where no candidate got more then 50% of the votes cast, including the election for the state’s sole representative in Congress.

One of those candidates, Eric Hafner, was apparently also included on the ballot in an attempt to confuse voters. Hafner, who was allowed to contest the race as a Democrat, over the objections of the state’s Democratic party, and despite having no connection to the state and currently being incarcerated in federal prison in New York, got 22,715 votes.
Had all of his ballots been cast for Hill, who was backed by the state’s Democratic party, Hill would have defeated Begich.
body_zh: 特朗普司法部采取行动，放弃对玛丽·佩尔托拉在阿拉斯加州参议院获胜的法律挑战2026 年美国中期选举
如果民主党赢得了两位名为丹·沙利文的候选人的竞选，总统曾试图阻止选举结果
在周四提交的一份法律文件中，特朗普政府要求联邦上诉法院驳回其在中期选举前提起的诉讼，该诉讼旨在阻止民主党人玛丽·佩尔托拉获胜后对阿拉斯加美国参议院竞选的认证。
法律挑战的焦点是第二位与现任共和党参议员丹·沙利文同名的候选人出现在选票上。阿拉斯加州最高法院已经裁定第二任沙利文的候选人资格合法，可以参加投票。
参议院共和党人拒绝停止伊朗战斗的战争权力法案
佩尔托拉确实以 50.13% 的得票率赢得了选举，这比所有其他候选人的得票总数还要多，其中包括现任共和党参议员丹·沙利文和第二位丹尼尔·沙利文，据报道，丹尼尔·沙利文是被民主党招募参加竞选的，目的是从现任参议员手中夺取选票。
该诉讼是在唐纳德·特朗普的指示下提起的，特朗普表示，在调查确定选民是否感到困惑之前，不应认证佩尔托拉的胜利。鉴于投票的保密性，政府从未解释如何进行此类调查。
比赛结果两天后，政府于周四采取行动，让上诉法院宣布该案没有实际意义。
《纽约时报》报道佩尔托拉的工作人员参与了招募“诱饵”丹·沙利文的计划后，佩尔托拉在竞选过程中面临重大争议。
佩尔托拉否认参与鼓励沙利文的第二次跑步。
佩尔托拉是尤皮克人，她将与奥及布威白土乐队成员、明尼苏达州当选参议员佩吉·弗拉纳根 (Peggy Flanagan) 一起，成为首批在美国参议院任职的两名美国原住民女性。
该法律文件是在阿拉斯加州结束计票并使用排名选择表来决定没有候选人获得超过 50% 选票的竞选（包括选举该州在国会的唯一代表）的一天后提交的。
其中一位候选人埃里克·哈夫纳（Eric Hafner）显然也被列入选票，试图迷惑选民。哈夫纳不顾该州民主党的反对，被允许作为民主党人参加竞选，尽管他与该州没有任何关系，目前被关押在纽约联邦监狱，但他获得了 22,715 票。
如果他的所有选票都投给了得到该州民主党支持的希尔，希尔就会击败贝吉奇。

body_en: 'Bigger than Barack Obama's election': Scholars reflect on Mississippi Senate race Scott Colom is now this Southern state's first Black U.S. senator in nearly 150 years. Scholars and Mississippi natives Eddie Glaude and Kiese Laymon discuss the historic significance of his victory.

Scott Colom is now this Southern state's first Black U.S. senator in nearly 150 years. Scholars and Mississippi natives Eddie Glaude and Kiese Laymon discuss the historic significance of his victory.

This is FRESH AIR. I'm Tonya Mosley. In the final weeks of Mississippi's Senate race, Democrat Scott Colom showed up outside a Donald Trump rally for his opponent and started talking to voters waiting to get in. He spent more than a year traveling across Mississippi, trying to convince people he could win, and last week, he did. Three years earlier, his opponent, Cindy Hyde-Smith, had blocked Colom's nomination to become a federal judge. Now he's headed to Washington to take her seat in the Senate.

But there's a much longer history behind the victory. Colom is a seventh-generation Mississippian, descended from an enslaved woman. He's now the state's first Black U.S. senator in nearly a hundred and fifty years. It's a remarkable moment in a state where Black political power was once built, then violently dismantled in the years after Reconstruction. During the Great Migration, generations of Black Americans, including my family, fled Mississippi to escape Jim Crow and racial terror. Others, like Colom's family, stayed and fought for change.

My guests today are two sons of Mississippi who have spent their lives examining the place they call home. Eddie Glaude is a professor of African American studies at Princeton University and grew up in Moss Point, a small town on the state's Gulf Coast. Writer Kiese Laymon grew up in the state's capital of Jackson. He's the author of the memoir "Heavy" and a professor of creative writing at Rice University. Kiese and Eddie, welcome to FRESH AIR.
KIESE LAYMON: Good to be here with y'all. Thank you.

MOSLEY: Well, Eddie, I want to start with you. When Colom won, you talked about being that little boy growing up in Moss Point, who never could have imagined a moment like this. And now we are here. And I'm actually just wondering, at what point in this race did you start to believe that it was possible?

GLAUDE: When the state of Mississippi hinted that it was about to redistrict, that they were going to engage in that project of gerrymandering that Donald Trump called for, there were these marches all throughout the South, and they were organized under the banner, All Roads Lead to the South. And Derrick Johnson gave me a call. He's the president and CEO of the NAACP, and I think in addition to that, he is the former president of the Mississippi chapter of the NAACP.

So he gave me a call and asked me to come down to Jackson to participate in the march there. And I did. And I was overwhelmed. I saw the organizing. I saw the infrastructure. I saw young people and older folk. And one of the things I did not hear was just this kind of nostalgic longing for the movement of the mid-20th century. What I heard instead and saw was organizing. They were counting. They were doing the math, Tonya. How many people do we need to turn out in DeSoto? How many people do we need to turn out in Holmes, in Jackson County, you know, in Hinds?

And what was so fascinating is that I knew then - and I was on stage with Congressman Bennie Thompson and Scott Colom. And I heard Scott speak, and I believed at that moment that he had a chance. You know, he's a political athlete, that's clear. But what was clearer to me was that these folks were ready. They were coming after us, and they were about to see the full weight and power of Black voters in Mississippi. They were going to undermine the math that was informing the redistricting effort. So I looked at Scott, and I looked at him closely, and I listened and, you know, I felt that Mississippi charm, and I said...
GLAUDE: ...OK. All right. We about to shock the world up in here.

MOSLEY: Kiese, how would you describe the mobilization, what it looked like on the ground there that maybe the national audience didn't really see? We just kind of - we know about the win and that there was a great mobilization.
LAYMON: I think that's a great question. You know, one of the things I think with this particular mobilization, unlike what we saw with Espy, and this goes to...
MOSLEY: And Espy - just to describe who Espy - Mike Espy...
MOSLEY: ...Actually ran against Hyde-Smith...

LAYMON: Right, ran against Cindy Hyde-Smith a few years ago. I worked hard on that campaign. I was living in Oxford at the time. I remember one morning, and Espy's - I don't want to say this person's name, but Espy's primary donor knocked on my door, sat on my porch. And the thing he was trying to, like, get me to understand was that we have to get Mike to let his hands go. That's what he kept saying. We have to let Mike let his hands go.

Now, Mike Espy, I think we need to understand - this is important for what Scott Colom did - was seen as a traditional, clean, electable Democrat, meaning that the people who put Mike Espy forward did not think he would offend many Republicans. What I loved about what Scott was doing this year was Scott, I think, took off that cloak of what some people call political respectability in terms of the look. And that was part of the galvanization. And so when I realized that Scott could win was when I saw, obviously, the commercial, the pick-a-protein commercial. Now, for me, I thought, Scott - my mother is a political scientist. She said, Kiese, I think Scott's going to have the votes. But in Mississippi, having the votes doesn't mean you're going to win.
body_zh: “比巴拉克·奥巴马的选举更重要”：学者们反思密西西比州参议员竞选斯科特·科洛姆现在是这个南方州近 150 年来第一位黑人美国参议员。学者们和密西西比人埃迪·格劳德和基泽·雷蒙讨论了他的胜利的历史意义。
您的支持有助于我们的演出成为可能，并解锁我们的无赞助商动态。
斯科特·科洛姆现在是这个南方州近 150 年来第一位黑人美国参议员。学者们和密西西比人埃迪·格劳德和基泽·雷蒙讨论了他的胜利的历史意义。
这是新鲜空气。我是托尼娅·莫斯利。在密西西比州参议院竞选的最后几周，民主党人斯科特·科洛姆出现在唐纳德·特朗普为对手举行的集会外，并开始与等待入场的选民交谈。他花了一年多的时间穿越密西西比州，试图说服人们他可以获胜，上周他做到了。三年前，他的对手辛迪·海德·史密斯（Cindy Hyde-Smith）阻止了科罗姆成为联邦法官的提名。现在他将前往华盛顿接替她在参议院的席位。
但这场胜利背后还有更悠久的历史。科罗姆是第七代密西西比人，是一名奴隶妇女的后裔。他现在是该州近一百五十年来第一位黑人美国参议员。在这个曾经建立过黑人政治权力，又在重建后的几年里被暴力拆除的州里，这是一个非凡的时刻。在大迁徙期间，几代美国黑人，包括我的家人，逃离密西西比州，以逃避种族歧视和种族恐怖。其他人，比如科罗姆的家人，留下来并为变革而奋斗。
今天我的客人是密西西比州的两个儿子，他们一生都在审视这个他们称之为家的地方。埃迪·格劳德是普林斯顿大学非裔美国人研究教授，在该州墨西哥湾沿岸的一个小镇莫斯波因特长大。作家基斯·雷蒙 (Kiese Laymon) 在该州首府杰克逊长大。他是回忆录《Heavy》的作者，也是莱斯大学创意写作教授。基斯和埃迪，欢迎来到新鲜空气。
KIESE LAYMON： 很高兴和大家在一起。谢谢。
莫斯利：埃迪，我想从你开始。当科罗姆获胜时，你谈到了在莫斯波因特长大的那个小男孩，他从来没有想象过这样的时刻。现在我们在这里。我其实只是想知道，在这场比赛中你从什么时候开始相信这是可能的？
格劳德：当密西西比州暗示即将重新划分选区，他们将参与唐纳德·特朗普所呼吁的不公正划分选区的项目时，整个南方都发生了这些游行，他们是在“条条道路通南方”的旗帜下组织的。德里克·约翰逊给我打了电话。他是全国有色人种协进会的主席兼首席执行官，我认为除此之外，他还是全国有色人种协进会密西西比州分会的前主席。
于是他给我打电话，让我去杰克逊参加那里的游行。我做到了。我不知所措。我看到了组织。我看到了基础设施。我看到了年轻人和老年人。而我没有听到的事情之一就是这种对20世纪中叶运动的怀旧渴望。相反，我听到和看到的是组织。他们在数数。他们正在做数学计算，托尼娅。德索托需要多少人参加？在霍姆斯、杰克逊县、海因兹，我们需要有多少人参加？
令人着迷的是，我当时就知道了——我和国会议员本尼·汤普森和斯科特·科洛姆一起在台上。我听到斯科特说话，那一刻我相信他有机会。你知道，他是一名政治运动员，这一点很明显。但我更清楚的是，这些人已经准备好了。他们追随我们，他们即将看到密西西比州黑人选民的全部分量和力量。他们将破坏为选区重新划分工作提供信息的数学原理。所以我看着斯科特，我仔细地看着他，我听着，你知道，我感受到了密西西比的魅力，我说……
格洛德：……好吧。好的。我们即将震惊世界。
莫斯利：基泽，你会如何描述这次动员？全国观众可能没有真正看到的现场情况是什么样的？我们只是——我们知道胜利，并且有一场伟大的动员。
雷蒙：我认为这是一个很好的问题。你知道，我认为这次特殊动员的一件事，与我们在 Espy 中看到的不同，这会导致......
莫斯利：还有埃斯皮——只是为了描述谁是埃斯皮——迈克·埃斯皮……
莫斯利：……实际上是与海德史密斯竞争……
雷蒙：对，几年前与辛迪·海德·史密斯竞选。我为那次竞选付出了很大的努力。当时我住在牛津。我记得有一天早上，埃斯皮的——我不想说出这个人的名字，但埃斯皮的主要捐赠者敲了我的门，坐在我的门廊上。他想让我明白的是，我们必须让迈克放开他的手。这就是他一直说的。我们必须让迈克放开他的手。

现在，迈克·埃斯皮，我认为我们需要明白——这对斯科特·科洛姆所做的事情很重要——被视为传统、干净、可当选的民主党人，这意味着提出迈克·埃斯皮的人并不认为他会冒犯许多共和党人。我认为斯科特今年所做的事情让我喜欢的是，斯科特脱下了一些人所谓的政治尊严的外衣。这是电镀的一部分。因此，当我意识到斯科特可能获胜时，我显然看到了广告，即选择蛋白质的广告。现在，对我来说，斯科特——我的母亲是一位政治学家。她说，基斯，我认为斯科特会获得选票。但在密西西比州，拥有选票并不意味着你就会获胜。

body_en: Sean Cairncross exits after outages that sparked fierce criticism, with DoD official Kirsten Davies to take over

White House national ⁠cyber director Sean ⁠Cairncross ​was ousted from his job, a person close to the White House told Reuters on Thursday, ⁠days after tech outages hit US air travel, banking and national security systems.

Cairncross oversaw cybersecurity policy and ⁠strategy across the federal government. Department of Defense chief information officer ​Kirsten Davies will ‌assume the position ‌temporarily, according to the source.
“The president fully supported firing Sean ‌Cairncross from his position,” said the person, who spoke on condition of anonymity.
Cairncross declined to comment on his departure.

Axios first reported Cairncross’s departure from the White House, citing anonymous officials claiming White House chief of staff Stephen Miller pushed for the personnel change because Cairncross “lacked the strong cyber credentials to perform the job”.

Technology-related outages have hit regularly over the last week, including a nationwide halt to air travel, a Microsoft outage that ‌hit email services and a temporary disruption to the US National Security Agency’s network.

The Trump administration ​has faced criticism over its response to the outages. The top US intelligence official said on Wednesday the disruptions to critical systems over the past week were separate service ⁠outages associated with maintenance and technical changes and not a ​coordinated or ​state-sponsored attack.

Cairncross was an ​executive at the Republican National Committee before assuming ​the cyber director ‌role. His ​successor will need ​to be confirmed by the Senate, which will be controlled by Democrats beginning in January.
body_zh: 肖恩·凯恩克罗斯 (Sean Cairncross) 在引发激烈批评的停电事件后退出，国防部官员克尔斯滕·戴维斯 (Kirsten Davies) 接任
周四，一位接近白宫的人士告诉路透社，白宫国家网络主管肖恩·凯恩克罗斯 (Sean Cairncross) 被免职，几天前，技术中断袭击了美国航空旅行、银行和国家安全系统。
凯恩克罗斯负责监督整个联邦政府的网络安全政策和战略。据消息人士称，国防部首席信息官克尔斯滕·戴维斯将暂时担任该职位。
这位不愿透露姓名的人士表示：“总统完全支持解雇肖恩·凯恩克罗斯。”
凯恩克罗斯拒绝就他的离职发表评论。
Axios 首先报道了凯恩克罗斯离开白宫的消息，并援引匿名官员的话称，白宫办公厅主任斯蒂芬·米勒推动了人事变动，因为凯恩克罗斯“缺乏强大的网络资历来执行这项工作”。
过去一周，与技术相关的中断经常发生，包括全国范围内的航空旅行暂停、微软电子邮件服务中断以及美国国家安全局网络的暂时中断。
特朗普政府因其对停电的反应而面临批评。美国最高情报官员周三表示，过去一周对关键系统的干扰是与维护和技术变更相关的单独服务中断，而不是协调或国家支持的攻击。
凯恩克罗斯在担任网络总监一职之前曾是共和党全国委员会的高管。他的继任者需要得到参议院的确认，参议院将从一月份开始由民主党控制。

body_en: Trump’s pick to lead election security agency says Jan. 6 was not an ‘attack’

The nominee selected by President Donald Trump to lead the agency tasked with protecting elections in the U.S. refused Thursday to answer who won the 2020 presidential election or call the riot on Jan. 6, 2021, “an attack.”

Michael LoSapio, who is nominated to lead the Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency, was pressed by Sen. Richard Blumenthal, D-Conn., on the issues during a confirmation hearing before the Senate Homeland Security Committee.
Asked specifically who won the presidential race in 2020, LoSapio said, “I’m not going to answer the question about an election six years ago.”
“My only involvement in the 2020 election was voting for the president of the United States,” he added, referencing Trump.
Blumenthal accused LoSapio of “ducking the question in a way that betrays your lack of independence and objectivity.”
CISA has not had a director confirmed by the Senate since Trump returned to office in January 2025, when Jen Easterly vacated the role.
The agency, which was established during the first Trump administration, was meant to protect the country’s critical infrastructure, including its elections, from hackers or cybercriminals.
LoSapio, who serves as the chief information security officer at data and software company Palantir, was also asked whether there was an attack on the Capitol on Jan. 6.
Blumenthal pressed him on the issue, saying, “You don’t know?”
“No, I don’t believe it was an attack,” LoSapio said. “I wasn’t involved in politics. I know what I saw on the news.”
Blumenthal asked LoSapio about the nature of the riot once again, to which he maintained that “it was not an attack.”
Trump’s own account of Jan. 6 has changed over the years , as he initially sought to distance himself from the riot, calling what happened “acts of violence and destruction” on Jan. 7, 2021.

Though, as he hit the campaign trail in 2024, Trump shifted gears to call it a “day of love,” and later, when he returned to office, he pardoned roughly 1,500 people and commuted the sentences of another 14 in connection with the attack. Trump’s Justice Department also tried to launch a controversial “anti-weaponization” fund, which critics have called a “slush fund” to compensate the president’s allies.
LoSapio is one of 13 nominees who appeared before the committee Thursday seeking to take over federal oversight, inspector general, Postal Service and District of Columbia Superior Court positions.

To be confirmed as CISA director, LoSapio requires the committee to vote to advance his nomination to the full Senate, whose vote by a simple majority will determine whether he is confirmed. The clock is ticking for Trump nominees, as Democrats will take over control of Congress in January.
The result of the 2020 presidential election has shaped CISA’s leadership. Trump fired its first director , Chris Krebs, just weeks after the election over his assertion that it was a secure race.
LoSapio isn’t the first Trump nominee to skirt around questions regarding 2020’s presidential race.
On Wednesday, Cody Hiland, Trump’s pick for a federal appeals court seat, told Blumenthal, “I’m not going to answer that,” when asked who won the election.
Asked why he would not answer, Hiland said, “Because it’s going down a political track on an issue that happened six years ago, and I don’t want to come close to an ethical violation.”
body_zh: 特朗普选择领导选举安全机构称 1 月 6 日不是“攻击”
唐纳德·特朗普总统选定领导负责保护美国选举的机构的提名人周四拒绝回答谁赢得了 2020 年总统选举，也拒绝将 2021 年 1 月 6 日的骚乱称为“袭击”。
被提名领导网络安全和基础设施安全局的迈克尔·洛萨皮奥(Michael LoSapio)在参议院国土安全委员会举行的确认听证会上受到康涅狄格州民主党参议员理查德·布卢门撒尔(Richard Blumenthal)的压力。
当被具体问及谁赢得了 2020 年总统竞选时，洛萨皮奥表示，“我不会回答有关六年前选举的问题。”
“我唯一参与 2020 年选举的就是投票给美国总统，”他补充道，他指的是特朗普。
布卢门撒尔指责洛萨皮奥“以一种暴露出你缺乏独立性和客观性的方式回避问题”。
自特朗普于 2025 年 1 月重返办公室、珍·伊斯特利 (Jen Easterly) 辞去该职务以来，CISA 尚未有一位经参议院确认的董事。
该机构是在特朗普第一届政府期间成立的，旨在保护该国的关键基础设施（包括选举）免受黑客或网络犯罪分子的侵害。
担任数据和软件公司 Palantir 首席信息安全官的 LoSapio 也被问及 1 月 6 日国会大厦是否遭到袭击。
布卢门撒尔在这个问题上向他施压，说道：“你不知道吗？”
“不，我不认为这是一次袭击，”洛萨皮奥说。 “我没有参与政治。我知道我在新闻中看到了什么。”
布卢门撒尔再次向洛萨皮奥询问骚乱的性质，他坚称“这不是袭击”。
特朗普本人对 1 月 6 日的描述多年来发生了变化，因为他最初试图与骚乱保持距离，称 2021 年 1 月 7 日发生的事件是“暴力和破坏行为”。
不过，在 2024 年开始竞选活动时，特朗普转变了态度，将这一天称为“爱的一天”，后来，当他重返办公室时，他赦免了大约 1,500 人，并对另外 14 名与袭击事件有关的人进行了减刑。特朗普的司法部还试图启动一项有争议的“反武器化”基金，批评者称其为“行贿基金”，以补偿总统的盟友。
LoSapio 是周四出现在委员会面前寻求接任联邦监督、监察长、邮政服务和哥伦比亚特区高等法院职位的 13 名提名人之一。
为了被确认为 CISA 主任，LoSapio 要求委员会投票将他的提名推进参议院全体会议，参议院的简单多数投票将决定他是否获得确认。特朗普提名人的时间已经不多了，民主党将于一月份接管国会。
2020 年主席选举的结果决定了 CISA 的领导层。特朗普在大选后几周解雇了第一任董事克里斯·克雷布斯(Chris Krebs)，因为他声称这是一场安全的竞选。
LoSapio 并不是第一个回避 2020 年总统竞选问题的特朗普提名人。
周三，特朗普提名的联邦上诉法院席位科迪·希兰在被问及谁赢得了选举时告诉布卢门撒尔，“我不会回答这个问题”。
当被问及为什么他不回答时，海兰德说，“因为六年前发生的问题正在走上政治轨道，我不想接近道德违规。”

title_en: Donald Trump issues posthumous pardon to MLB ‘superstar and legend’ Pete Rose
title_zh: 唐纳德·特朗普对美国职业棒球大联盟“超级巨星和传奇人物”皮特·罗斯给予死后赦免
summary: Rose pleaded guilty to tax evasion in 1990 Player also banned from baseball over bets Donald Trump says he has posthumously pardoned Pete Rose more than two years after the baseball star’s death and a year after he was reinstated by Major League Baseball Commi
summary_zh: 罗斯承认 1990 年逃税罪 球员还因打赌而被禁止参加棒球 唐纳德·特朗普表示，他在死后赦免了皮特·罗斯
body_en: Donald Trump says he has posthumously pardoned Pete Rose more than two years after the baseball star’s death and a year after he was reinstated by Major League Baseball Commissioner Rob Manfred.
“I have just given a Complete and Total Pardon to the Late, Great Pete Rose, a true Baseball SUPERSTAR + LEGEND,” Trump posted on social media.
Charlie Hustle: the definitive Pete Rose book that deconstructs a disgraced legend

Rose, MLB’s career hits leader, entered guilty pleas in April 1990 to two counts of filing false tax returns, admitting he failed to report $354,968 during a four-year period. Facing a sentence of up to six years in prison and $500,000 in fines, Rose was sentenced to five months in prison. Rose also repaid the Internal Revenue Service $366,042.

The pleas came eight months after Rose agreed to a permanent ban from baseball . He agreed to the ban after an MLB investigation concluded he bet numerous times on the Cincinnati Reds while playing on and managing his hometown team from 1985-87. ″I know I’m not a bad person, but I did make some mistakes and it’s in the eyes of the judge,″ Rose said on the day he was banned from baseball. ″All you can say is it’s up to the judge.″

The pardon comes after Manfred issued a sweeping decision last May that opened a pathway for Rose to be considered for baseball’s Hall of Fame. Manfred declared that individuals on MLB’s permanently ineligible list would have their statuses restored at death, a ruling that affected 17 people, most notably Rose and Shoeless Joe Jackson. The earliest Rose or Jackson could now be inducted into the Hall of Fame would be in 2028.

A 17-time All-Star during a playing career from 1963-86, Rose was the 1963 National League Rookie of the Year, 1973 MVP and 1975 World Series MVP. A three-time NL batting champion, he broke the prior hits record of 4,191 set by Ty Cobb from 1905-28.
body_zh: 唐纳德·特朗普表示，在棒球明星皮特·罗斯去世两年多后，以及美国职业棒球大联盟专员罗布·曼弗雷德恢复他的职位一年后，他已在死后赦免了皮特·罗斯。
特朗普在社交媒体上发帖称：“我刚刚对已故的伟大的皮特·罗斯进行了完全彻底的赦免，他是一位真正的棒球巨星+传奇人物。”
《查理骗局》：皮特·罗斯的权威著作，解构了一个不光彩的传奇
罗斯是美国职业棒球大联盟的职业打击领袖，他于 1990 年 4 月对两项提交虚假纳税申报表的罪名认罪，承认自己在四年内未申报 354,968 美元。罗斯被判处最高 6 年监禁和 50 万美元罚款，并被判处 5 个月监禁。罗斯还向国税局偿还了 366,042 美元。
罗斯同意永久禁止参加棒球比赛八个月后提出了这一请求。美国职业棒球大联盟（MLB）调查得出结论，他在 1985-87 赛季效力和管理家乡球队期间多次押注于辛辛那提红人队后，他同意了禁令。 “我知道我不是一个坏人，但我确实犯了一些错误，这在法官眼中，”罗斯在被禁止参加棒球比赛的那天说道。 “你只能说这取决于法官。”
曼弗雷德去年五月做出了一项全面决定，为罗斯进入棒球名人堂开辟了道路。曼弗雷德宣布，美国职业棒球大联盟永久不合格名单上的个人将在死亡后恢复其身份，这一裁决影响了 17 人，其中最著名的是罗斯和无鞋乔·杰克逊。罗斯或杰克逊最早可以在 2028 年入选名人堂。
罗斯在 1963-86 赛季的职业生涯中 17 次入选全明星，并荣获 1963 年国家联盟年度最佳新秀、1973 年 MVP 和 1975 年世界大赛 MVP。作为三届国联击球冠军，他打破了泰·科布 (Ty Cobb) 在 1905-28 年创下的 4,191 支安打纪录。

title_en: Senate Republicans rejects war powers bill to halt fighting in Iran
title_zh: 参议院共和党人拒绝停止伊朗战斗的战争权力法案
summary: Measure fails 48-51 with GOP members again defending war that played a role in costing them midterm elections The Senate on Thursday rejected a war powers resolution aimed at forcing Donald Trump to halt fighting with Iran, with Republicans once again defendin
summary_zh: 该措施以 48 比 51 失败，共和党成员再次捍卫战争，这场战争在他们中期选举中发挥了作用。参议院周四拒绝了一项战争政策
body_en: Measure fails 48-51 with GOP members again defending war that played a role in costing them midterm elections

The Senate on Thursday rejected a war powers resolution aimed at forcing Donald Trump to halt fighting with Iran, with Republicans once again defending a conflict that played a major role in their sweeping midterm election losses.

The House of Representatives had approved the resolution in September, and it was the first to be voted on by either chamber since the 3 November vote in which the GOP lost control of both chambers of Congress beginning next year.

The measure failed in a 48-51 vote that broke largely along party lines, with John Fetterman of Pennsylvania the sole Democrat to oppose it, and Susan Collins of Maine, Rand Paul of Kentucky and Lisa Murkowski of Alaska the only Republicans to vote in favor.

Democrats have introduced a steady stream of war powers resolutions since the war began in February with a joint US-Israel attack on Iran. While Trump’s Republican allies have succeeded in voting many of them down, one passed both chambers in June .

However Trump ignored that resolution, prompting Democrats to continue their efforts to make use of the 1973 law to force an end to a conflict that polls indicate is unpopular with the public and has caused prices for gasoline and diesel to increase across the US.

All House Democrats along with seven Republicans – several of whom lost re-election in the midterms – had supported the measure that came up for consideration before the Senate on Thursday. But Republicans largely stood behind the conflict, including Thom Tillis, a North Carolina senator, who is retiring at the end of the year after supporting previous resolutions, and Bill Cassidy, an outgoing senator of Louisiana, whose support was crucial for the June measure’s passage.
Chris Murphy, a Democratic senator, missed the vote, after recently suffering a stroke.
body_zh: 该措施以 48 比 51 失败，共和党成员再次捍卫战争，这场战争导致他们在中期选举中失败
参议院周四否决了一项旨在迫使唐纳德·特朗普停止与伊朗交战的战争权力决议，共和党人再次为一场冲突辩护，这场冲突在他们中期选举的全面失败中发挥了重要作用。
众议院于 9 月批准了该决议，这是自 11 月 3 日投票以来，共和党从明年开始失去对参众两院的控制权以来第一个由两院投票表决的决议。
该法案以 48 比 51 的投票结果失败，投票结果很大程度上打破了党派界限，宾夕法尼亚州的约翰·费特曼 (John Fetterman) 是唯一反对该法案的民主党人，缅因州的苏珊·柯林斯 (Susan Collins)、肯塔基州的兰德·保罗 (Rand Paul) 和阿拉斯加州的丽莎·穆尔科斯基 (Lisa Murkowski) 是唯一投赞成票的共和党人。
自二月份战争爆发以来，美国和以色列联合攻击伊朗，民主党不断提出战争权力决议。尽管特朗普的共和党盟友已成功否决了其中的许多议案，但其中一项议案于 6 月在参众两院获得通过。
然而特朗普忽视了这项决议，促使民主党人继续努力利用 1973 年的法律来强制结束一场冲突，民调显示这场冲突不受公众欢迎，并导致美国各地汽油和柴油价格上涨。
所有众议院民主党人和七名共和党人（其中几人在中期选举中失去连任）都支持周四提交参议院审议的这项措施。但共和党人在很大程度上支持这场冲突，其中包括北卡罗来纳州参议员汤姆·蒂利斯(Thom Tillis)，他在支持之前的决议后将于今年年底退休，以及即将卸任的路易斯安那州参议员比尔·卡西迪(Bill Cassidy)，他的支持对于六月法案的通过至关重要。
民主党参议员克里斯·墨菲最近中风后错过了投票。

title_en: Trump’s CISA pick rejects Jan. 6 as an 'attack,' won't name 2020 election winner
title_zh: 特朗普的 CISA 人选将 1 月 6 日视为“攻击”，不会提名 2020 年大选获胜者
summary: Michael LoSapio, President Donald Trump's nominee to lead the Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency, says he doesn't consider the Jan_ 6 Capitol insurrection an "attack."
summary_zh: 唐纳德·特朗普总统提名的网络安全和基础设施安全局局长迈克尔·洛萨皮奥 (Michael LoSapio) 表示，他不考虑 1 月 6 日的法案
body_en: Michael LoSapio, President Donald Trump's nominee to lead the Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency, says he doesn't consider the Jan_ 6 Capitol insurrection an "attack."

President Donald Trump's pick to lead an agency with a key role in protecting U.S. elections told senators during a confirmation hearing Thursday that he wouldn't characterize the Jan. 6, 2021, U.S. Capitol insurrection as an “attack."

The response by Michael LoSapio, nominated to head the Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency, came as part of an exchange with U.S. Sen. Richard Blumenthal, D-Conn., who has made inquiries about the violence and the 2020 election part of his line of questioning for a number of Trump nominees.
It's also part of Republicans' rush to confirm Trump's picks before Democrats take power in Congress early next year.
“No, I don’t believe it was an attack,” LoSapio told Blumenthal. “I wasn’t involved in politics. I know what I saw on the news.”

The White House did not immediately return a request seeking comment on the remark by LoSapio, who if confirmed would inherit an agency mired in partisan tensions over the role it should play in combating false claims about voting or election fraud.
He also isn't the first Trump nominee to answer the Jan. 6 question similarly.

During his own June confirmation hearing for the post of Department of Justice inspector general, Don R. Berthiaume — also during questioning from Blumenthal — acknowledged “violence on the Capitol grounds” on Jan. 6, 2021, but also said, “I don’t know if I would use the term attack.”
Several of Trump's judicial nominees have also shied away from characterizing the violence as an “attack” during their own confirmation hearings.

On Thursday, Blumenthal also asked LoSapio, currently chief information security officer at artificial intelligence firm Palantir, who won the popular vote in the 2020 presidential election, which Trump has falsely claimed that he won.

“I’m not going to answer the question about an election six years ago,” LoSapio said, later adding that his “only involvement” in that election was voting for Trump.

CISA — formed in 2018 during the first Trump administration and nested within the Department of Homeland Security — is charged with protecting the nation’s critical infrastructure, from dams and nuclear power plants to banks and voting systems.

It's received bipartisan praise from many state and local election officials, but Trump and his allies remain angry over its efforts to counter misinformation about the 2020 presidential election and the coronavirus pandemic.
The agency’s first director, Chris Krebs, was fired by Trump after highlighting election officials' statement calling the 2020 election the " most secure in American history.”

CISA has also been without a Senate-confirmed director for nearly two years. Jen Easterly left the agency as Trump returned to office last year, and Nick Andersen has led the agency in an acting capacity since February. Sean Plankey withdrew in April when his nomination stalled.

被提名为网络安全和基础设施安全局局长的迈克尔·洛萨皮奥 (Michael LoSapio) 的回应是与康涅狄格州民主党参议员理查德·布卢门撒尔 (Richard Blumenthal) 交流的一部分。布卢门撒尔在对多位特朗普提名人进行质询时，曾就暴力事件和 2020 年大选进行过询问。
这也是共和党在民主党明年初在国会掌权之前急于确认特朗普选择的一部分。

白宫没有立即回复要求对洛萨皮奥的言论发表评论的请求，如果洛萨皮奥的言论得到证实，他将继承一个陷入党派紧张关系的机构，该机构在打击有关投票或选举舞弊的虚假指控方面应发挥作用。

特朗普的几位司法提名人在自己的确认听证会上也回避将暴力事件定性为“袭击”。
周四，布卢门撒尔还询问了现任人工智能公司 Palantir 首席信息安全官的 LoSapio，他在 2020 年总统选举中赢得了普选，而特朗普谎称自己赢得了这次选举。

title_en: Judges have put Trump's arch and golf course on hold, but only for a matter of days
title_zh: 法官暂停了特朗普的拱门和高尔夫球场，但只持续了几天
summary: A federal judge has twice delayed construction of Trump's arch. Another is keeping East Potomac Park open. The proposed golf course redesign got mixed feedback from a federal arts panel on Thursday.
summary_zh: 一名联邦法官曾两次推迟特朗普拱门的建设。另一个是保持东波托马克公园开放。拟议的高尔夫球场重新设计方案褒贬不一
body_en: Courts temporarily block Trump arch, golf course work : NPR

Courts temporarily block Trump arch, golf course work A federal judge has twice delayed construction of Trump's arch. Another is keeping East Potomac Park open. The proposed golf course redesign got mixed feedback from a federal arts panel on Thursday.
Federal judges have issued temporary restraining orders to block construction of Trump's arch and keep East Potomac Park open. Julia Demaree Nikhinson/AP hide caption
A federal judge has extended her block on construction of President Trump's D.C. arch for two weeks, another short-term victory for those who don't want to see the 250-foot structure break ground.

D.C. District Judge Tanya Chutkan extended her temporary restraining order on Wednesday, the day before it was set to expire. She originally stepped in to block construction on the night of Nov. 5, after the National Capital Planning Commission and National Park Service gave the arch final approval and the Trump administration said construction could begin imminently.
Democrats want to stop Trump's arch, golf course and more. What are their options?

Chutkan's new five-page order prevents the administration from "initiating, making, or otherwise effectuating any construction, excavation, demolition, land-disturbance, utility-installation, or roadway-closure activity, or any other construction-related activity" at Memorial Circle through Dec. 3.

"The judge's order recognizes that the conditions that called for emergency relief two weeks ago remain unchanged," Nick Sansone, the Public Citizen attorney representing the original plaintiffs in the lawsuit, said in a statement .
The extension gives Chutkan more time to consider plaintiffs' request for a longer-term preliminary injunction, which would prohibit construction as the lawsuit against the arch plays out.
That lawsuit started earlier this year with a challenge from a group of Vietnam War veterans and an architectural historian, but has expanded in recent weeks.

In late October, the governments of D.C. and Virginia filed another lawsuit, which was combined with the original. And nine members of the Kennedy family joined the fight last week, saying the arch will block historic sightlines and cast shadows over the graves of John F. Kennedy and others at nearby Arlington National Cemetery.
Kennedy relatives join the fight against Trump's arch, alleging harm to JFK's grave

"This is one man who wants to build this arch. He's violated every rule. If this is a great idea, then bring it before Congress, follow the rules and get it approved," Max Kennedy, a son of Robert F. Kennedy, told NPR's All Things Considered .
Opposition to the arch — from area residents, veterans, local officials, Democratic lawmakers and more — has grown in recent months as the structure hurtled through the federal approval process.

Critics take issue with the arch's scale and location , saying it would interrupt the solemn and historic vista between Arlington National Cemetery and the Lincoln Memorial. Plaintiffs argue the structure violates several laws — including the Commemorative Works Act and D.C.'s Height of Buildings Act — and is fundamentally illegal without approval from Congress.
A jogger passes a mobile security camera truck at Memorial Circle, where Trump wants to build his arch. Tom Brenner/AP hide caption
The Trump administration has not sought that approval, arguing the arch is covered by Congress' authorization in 1925 of a pair of 166-foot columns at the same location, which were never built.

In court filings and a recently unveiled website , the administration characterizes building the arch as a matter of urgency — both to complete that century-old vision and to facilitate national security . Trump said in September that the arch would double as a military complex, but the plans that got final approval this month don't include any details to that effect.

In a declaration this week , Ricky Buria, chief of staff to Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth, told the court that the agency is "currently in the planning process to determine how to integrate national defense uses … into the Arch without changing the existing plans for the Arch."
body_zh: 法院暂时封锁特朗普拱门和高尔夫球场工作：NPR
法院暂时封锁特朗普拱门、高尔夫球场工程一名联邦法官两次推迟特朗普拱门的建设。另一个是保持东波托马克公园开放。周四，拟议的高尔夫球场重新设计得到了联邦艺术小组的不同反馈。
联邦法官已发布临时限制令，以阻止特朗普拱门的建设并保持东波托马克公园的开放。朱莉娅·德玛丽·尼金森/美联社隐藏标题栏
一名联邦法官将特朗普总统华盛顿拱门的建设禁令延长了两周，对于那些不想看到这座 250 英尺高的建筑破土动工的人来说，这又是一次短期胜利。
华盛顿地区法官塔尼娅·查特坎 (Tanya Chutkan) 于周三延长了临时限制令，即临时限制令到期的前一天。在国家首都规划委员会和国家公园管理局给予拱门最终批准以及特朗普政府表示施工可以立即开始之后，她最初于 11 月 5 日晚介入阻止施工。
民主党人希望阻止特朗普的拱门、高尔夫球场等。他们的选择是什么？
Chutkan 的新的五页命令禁止政府在 12 月 3 日之前在纪念圆环“启动、进行或以其他方式实施任何建筑、挖掘、拆除、土地扰动、公用设施安装或道路封闭活动，或任何其他与建筑相关的活动”。
代表诉讼原告的公共公民律师尼克·桑索在一份声明中表示：“法官的命令承认两周前要求紧急救济的条件保持不变。”
延期使楚特坎有更多时间考虑原告提出的长期初步禁令的请求，该禁令将在针对拱门的诉讼结束后禁止施工。
该诉讼于今年早些时候开始，由一群越南战争退伍军人和一位建筑历史学家发起挑战，但最近几周有所扩大。
10月下旬，华盛顿特区和弗吉尼亚州政府又提起了另一起诉讼，该诉讼与原来的诉讼合并在一起。肯尼迪家族的九名成员上周也加入了这场战斗，称拱门将挡住历史视线，并在附近阿灵顿国家公墓的约翰·F·肯尼迪和其他人的坟墓上投下阴影。
肯尼迪亲属加入反对特朗普拱门的斗争，声称肯尼迪坟墓遭到破坏
“这是一个想要建造这座拱门的人。他违反了每一条规则。如果这是一个好主意，那么就将其提交给国会，遵守规则并获得批准，”罗伯特·F·肯尼迪的儿子马克斯·肯尼迪告诉美国国家公共广播电台的所有事情考虑。
近几个月来，随着该建筑迅速通过联邦审批程序，来自当地居民、退伍军人、地方官员、民主党议员等的反对声音有所增加。
批评者对拱门的规模和位置提出质疑，称它会破坏阿灵顿国家公墓和林肯纪念堂之间庄严且历史悠久的景观。原告辩称，该建筑违反了多项法律——包括《纪念工程法》和华盛顿特区的《建筑高度法》——并且未经国会批准根本上是非法的。
一名慢跑者经过纪念圆环上的一辆移动安全摄像车，特朗普想在那里建造他的拱门。汤姆·布伦纳/美联社隐藏标题栏
特朗普政府并未寻求批准，称拱门是由国会于 1925 年授权在同一地点建造一对 166 英尺高的柱子覆盖的，但这些柱子从未建成。
在法庭文件和最近公布的网站中，政府将建造这座拱门视为紧急事项——既是为了完成这个百年愿景，也是为了促进国家安全。特朗普在九月表示，拱门将兼作军事设施，但本月获得最终批准的计划并未包含任何相关细节。
在本周的一份声明中，国防部长皮特·赫格斯的幕僚长里基·布里亚告诉法庭，该机构“目前正在规划过程中，以确定如何将国防用途……整合到拱门中，而不改变拱门的现有计划。”

summary_zh: 据报道，比尔·埃萨利 (Bill Essayli) 被派往佛罗里达州，对杰克·史密斯 (Jack Smith) 处理机密文件案件的情况进行刑事调查
body_en: DoJ assigns pro-Trump prosecutor to handle inquiry into 2022 Mar-a-Lago raid, reports say | Trump administration
Bill Essayli reportedly dispatched to Florida to handle a criminal inquiry into Jack Smith’s handling of the classified documents case

The US Department of Justice is, according to reports, dispatching Bill Essayli, a California prosecutor who is a staunch ally of the president, to Florida to handle a criminal inquiry into one of Donald Trump’s obsessions: the 2022 search of Mar-a-Lago and Jack Smith’s handling of the classified documents case.

The decision to dispatch Essayli comes as a broad criminal investigation into whether Obama and Biden administration officials violated Trump’s rights has stalled in the US attorney’s office for the southern district of Florida . Jason Reding Quiñones, the US attorney for the office, resigned earlier this month. Other prosecutors working on the case have resigned.

Essayli’s assignment was first reported by Politico. The New York Times and Bloomberg Law have also reported Essayli’s transfer. Justice department spokespeople did not immediately respond to inquiries on Thursday.

Trump has long raged about the raid, framing his 2024 presidential run in part as vengeance over what he asserts was political persecution under the Biden justice department. He has called the Mar-a-Lago raid a “ siege ” and Smith a “ sick son of a bitch .”

News of his Florida position comes weeks after a federal judge ruled that Essayli was “ unlawfully serving ” as the head of the US attorney’s office in Los Angeles and should be disqualified from overseeing two criminal prosecutions.

Essayli was not formally nominated by Trump, but appointed “interim” US attorney in April 2025, allowing him to head the office without Senate confirmation. The Trump administration has since kept him in the top position with a “first assistant” title, and defense lawyers have fought for months to have him removed. The judge’s recent disqualification ruling is under appeal.

Essayli, a Trump loyalist, has made national headlines pursuing cases that closely align with the Maga agenda . Over the last year, his office has aggressively prosecuted protesters and local residents for alleged crimes against immigration officers, including “conspiring” against and “impeding” agents. But the Guardian recently found that as of mid-September, out of more than 100 cases, the majority have ended in dismissals, acquittals or misdemeanor pleas.

In the lead up to the midterms, Essayli tried to force California election officials to set aside thousands of ballots, alleging widespread voter fraud, but was repeatedly blocked by the courts, and state officials said he was spreading misinformation and risked disenfranchising voters.
Before he headed the US attorney’s office in LA, Essayli was a Republican state lawmaker who railed against “woke” California policies and fought to undo trans rights.
body_zh: 报道称，美国司法部指派亲特朗普检察官处理 2022 年海湖庄园袭击事件的调查特朗普政府
据报道，比尔·埃萨利被派往佛罗里达州，对杰克·史密斯处理机密文件案的情况进行刑事调查
据报道，美国司法部正派遣总统的坚定盟友、加利福尼亚州检察官比尔·埃萨利 (Bill Essayli) 前往佛罗里达州，对唐纳德·特朗普的一项痴迷事项进行刑事调查：2022 年对海湖庄园的搜查和杰克·史密斯处理机密文件案的情况。
在做出派遣埃萨利的决定之际，美国佛罗里达州南部地区检察官办公室对奥巴马和拜登政府官员是否侵犯特朗普权利的广泛刑事调查陷入僵局。该办公室的美国检察官杰森·雷丁·奎尼奥内斯(Jason Reding Quiñones)本月早些时候辞职。其他负责此案的检察官已辞职。
埃萨利的任命最先由 Politico 报道。 《纽约时报》和《彭博社法律》也报道了埃萨利的调动。司法部发言人周四没有立即回应询问。
特朗普长期以来一直对这次突袭感到愤怒，他将自己参加 2024 年总统竞选的部分原因归结为对他所称的拜登司法部门政治迫害的报复。他称海湖庄园的突袭是“围攻”，史密斯是“变态的王八蛋”。
几周前，一名联邦法官裁定埃萨利“非法担任”洛杉矶美国检察官办公室主任，并应取消监督两项刑事诉讼的资格。
埃萨利并未得到特朗普的正式提名，但于 2025 年 4 月被任命为“临时”美国检察官，使他无需参议院确认即可担任该办公室的负责人。此后，特朗普政府以“第一助理”头衔让他继续担任最高职位，辩护律师几个月来一直在努力将他免职。法官最近的取消资格裁决正在上诉。
埃萨利是特朗普的忠实拥护者，因追查与马加议程密切相关的案件而成为全国头条新闻。去年，他的办公室积极起诉抗议者和当地居民，指控他们对移民官员犯下罪行，包括“密谋”和“阻碍”特工。但《卫报》最近发现，截至9月中旬，在100多起案件中，大多数都以解雇、无罪释放或轻罪抗辩而告终。
在中期选举前夕，埃萨利试图迫使加州选举官员搁置数千张选票，指控其存在广泛的选民欺诈行为，但多次遭到法院阻止，州官员称他正在散布错误信息，并冒着剥夺选民选举权的风险。
在担任洛杉矶美国检察官办公室负责人之前，埃萨利是一名共和党州议员，他反对“觉醒”的加州政策，并为废除跨性别者权利而奋斗。

title_en: Trump accused of falling asleep during Xi Jinping speech at Apec summit in China
title_zh: 特朗普被指在习近平在中国亚太经合组织峰会上发表讲话时睡着了
summary: US president appeared to doze off while Chinese leader made speech, but White House insisted he was awake Donald Trump was, again, accused of falling asleep during a televised event, this time during the speech of the Chinese president, Xi Jinping, at the Asia
summary_zh: 中国领导人讲话时美国总统似乎打瞌睡，但白宫坚称他醒着 唐纳德·特朗普再次被指摔倒
body_en: Trump accused of falling asleep during Xi Jinping speech at Apec summit in China | Donald Trump
US president appeared to doze off while Chinese leader made speech, but White House insisted he was awake

Donald Trump was, again, accused of falling asleep during a televised event, this time during the speech of the Chinese president, Xi Jinping, at the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (Apec) summit in China.
The US president appeared to close his eyes for roughly 10 seconds on Thursday. As his eyes closed, Trump’s head tilted downward, and his hands remained clasped in front of him.
Global courts under attack and four more takeaways from the Trump, Xi, Putin meeting

Several prominent Trump critics on social media alleged that the US president was asleep, including Republicans Against Trump , California governor Gavin Newsom’s press office and conservative lawyer George Conway .
White House officials denied the allegations, claiming the 80-year-old US president was looking down at papers in front of him.

“Fake News! President Trump was looking at papers in front of him while the speaker made remarks. You can clearly see his eyes move back and forth,” Steven Cheung, the White House director of communications, wrote on X in response to a Newsweek article.
“This is why the people despise media so much. They constantly lie,” Cheung added.
Trump often faces accusations of falling asleep during televised events such as Oval Office press conferences, cabinet meetings and sporting events.

Occasionally, while listening to other people speak, the US president will close his eyes for several seconds, appearing as though he is falling asleep . Despite footage of the instances going viral, the White House and Trump allies have insisted the US president does not fall asleep during meetings.
Administration officials have excused Trump’s apparent drowsiness as blinking or an example of the president listening intently. They consistently claim Trump “doesn’t sleep”.
Marco Rubio, the US secretary of state, testified to lawmakers earlier this year that he had “never seen” Trump fall asleep.
“On the contrary, the guy doesn’t sleep, which is a big problem because he calls me at two in the morning,” Rubio said in June.
Last year, JD Vance said that Trump hardly ever sleeps, even while traveling overnight.
“If we go on a 20-hour trip somewhere, he doesn’t sleep the entire time. And of course, if he’s not sleeping, if he’s working, he expects everybody else to be working too,” Vance told Fox News .

Trump became the oldest US president ever inaugurated when he was sworn in nearly two years ago. Despite his age, Trump often claims he is in near-perfect health , often bragging about his “perfect” cognitive test results and insisting he has a lot of energy.
body_zh: 特朗普被指在习近平在中国亚太经合组织峰会上讲话时睡着了唐纳德·特朗普
中国领导人讲话时美国总统似乎打瞌睡，但白宫坚称他醒着
唐纳德·特朗普再次被指控在电视转播活动中睡着了，这次是在中国国家主席习近平在中国举行的亚太经合组织（APEC）峰会上发表讲话期间。
周四，这位美国总统似乎闭上了眼睛大约 10 秒钟。特朗普闭上眼睛，头低垂，双手仍握在身前。
全球法院受到攻击以及特朗普、习近平、普京会晤的另外四点收获
社交媒体上几位著名的特朗普批评者声称美国总统睡着了，其中包括反对特朗普的共和党人、加州州长加文·纽瑟姆的新闻办公室和保守派律师乔治·康威。
白宫官员否认了这些指控，称这位 80 岁的美国总统正在低头看着他面前的文件。
“假新闻！演讲者发表讲话时，特朗普总统正在看他面前的文件。你可以清楚地看到他的眼睛来回移动，”白宫通讯主管史蒂文·张 (Steven Cheung) 在 X 上回应《新闻周刊》的一篇文章时写道。
“这就是为什么人们如此鄙视媒体。他们总是撒谎，”张补充道。
特朗普经常面临在椭圆形办公室新闻发布会、内阁会议和体育赛事等电视活动中打瞌睡的指控。
偶尔，美国总统在听别人讲话时，会闭上眼睛几秒钟，看起来就像是睡着了。尽管这些事件的视频在网上疯传，但白宫和特朗普的盟友坚称美国总统在会议期间不会睡着。
政府官员将特朗普明显的困倦解释为眨眼或总统专心聆听的例子。他们一直声称特朗普“不睡觉”。
美国国务卿马可·卢比奥今年早些时候向议员作证说，他“从未见过”特朗普睡着。
“相反，这个人不睡觉，这是一个大问题，因为他凌晨两点给我打电话，”卢比奥在六月说道。
去年，JD 万斯表示，特朗普几乎从不睡觉，即使是在通宵旅行时也是如此。
“如果我们去某个地方进行 20 小时的旅行，他不会一直在睡觉。当然，如果他不睡觉，如果他在工作，他希望其他人也能工作，”万斯告诉福克斯新闻。
特朗普在近两年前宣誓就职时成为美国历史上年龄最大的总统。尽管年事已高，特朗普经常声称自己的健康状况近乎完美，经常吹嘘自己“完美”的认知测试结果，并坚称自己精力充沛。

title_en: Utah GOP governor on Trump and 2028: ‘It’s time for the next thing’
title_zh: 犹他州共和党州长谈特朗普和 2028 年：“是时候做下一步了”
summary: Gov. Spencer Cox said he’s 'a fan of governors' as he eyes the party’s options for a 2028 nominee.
summary_zh: 州长斯宾塞·考克斯 (Spencer Cox) 在考虑该党 2028 年提名人选时表示，他是“州长的粉丝”。
body_en: Utah’s Republican governor wants his party to move beyond President Donald Trump heading into the next presidential election.

“It’s time for the next thing,” Gov. Spencer Cox said in an interview on Wednesday at the POLITICO Pub, on the sidelines of the National Governors Association’s New Governors Leadership Forum in Deer Valley, Utah.
Cox called on his fellow Republicans to start looking for new leadership in the wake of this month’s midterm election defeats.
“This is how this works when presidents move on. We should be looking for the next leadership in our party and what that looks like,” Cox told POLITICO’s Samuel Benson.

“We’ve got JD Vance and Marco Rubio, and those seem to be kind of the two choices now,” Cox said, referring to the Vice President and Secretary of State, respectively. “But I think you’ll see a lot of people step up … there are a lot of really interesting folks.”
“I’m a fan of governors,” Cox added. “I think governors with executive experience are the best to lead the country.”

Vance told Fox News earlier this week that he would decide “sometime next year” whether he will run for president in 2028. Rubio has dismissed suggestions that he would launch his own bid, and has said he would support Vance if the Vice President ran for the White House.
“I am hopeful that there are some Republican governors that will throw their hat in,” said Cox, a two-term governor. “We can have a competition of ideas heading in to find out what's next.”

Cox said that Trump still has a “really important role to play” in leading the party over the next two years, adding that the president still had an “opportunity” to strike bipartisan deals on permitting reform and other policy areas in his last two years in office.
Cox called the president “unique,” adding: “He’s someone who has the attention of the country in a way that almost no president has had in my lifetime.”
“People really love him or really don’t like him, but everybody’s paying attention to him,” he said.
body_zh: 犹他州共和党州长希望他的政党在下届总统选举中超越唐纳德·特朗普总统。
周三，在犹他州鹿谷举行的全国州长协会新州长领导力论坛间隙，州长斯宾塞·考克斯在 POLITICO 酒吧接受采访时表示，“是时候做下一件事了。”
考克斯呼吁他的共和党同僚在本月中期选举失败后开始寻找新的领导层。
“这就是总统卸任时的运作方式。我们应该寻找党内的下一任领导层，以及他的样子，”考克斯告诉《政治》杂志的塞缪尔·本森。
“我们有 JD 万斯和马可·卢比奥，现在看来这就是两个选择，”考克斯分别指的是副总统和国务卿。 “但我认为你会看到很多人挺身而出……有很多非常有趣的人。”
“我是州长的粉丝，”考克斯补充道。 “我认为具有行政经验的州长是领导国家的最佳人选。”
万斯本周早些时候告诉福克斯新闻，他将在“明年某个时候”决定是否参加 2028 年总统竞选。卢比奥否认了他将自己竞选的建议，并表示如果副总统竞选白宫，他将支持万斯。
“我希望有一些共和党州长能够加入进来，”两届州长考克斯说。 “我们可以进行一场创意竞赛，看看接下来会发生什么。”
考克斯表示，特朗普在未来两年领导该党方面仍将发挥“非常重要的作用”，并补充说，总统在任期的最后两年仍有“机会”就允许改革和其他政策领域达成两党协议。
考克斯称这位总统“独一无二”，并补充道：“他受到了国家的关注，这是我一生中几乎没有一位总统受到关注的。”
“人们真的很爱他，或者真的不喜欢他，但每个人都在关注他，”他说。

title_en: Senate passes bipartisan permitting bill designed to boost energy projects
title_zh: 参议院通过旨在促进能源项目的两党许可法案
summary: The Senate approved a long-sought bipartisan permitting reform bill on Thursday, following a major breakthrough on legislation that aims to cut costs by ramping up the speed of infrastructure and energy projects.
summary_zh: 在旨在削减成本的立法取得重大突破之后，参议院周四批准了一项期待已久的两党许可改革法案
body_en: Washington — The Senate approved a long-sought bipartisan permitting reform bill on Thursday, following a major breakthrough on legislation that aims to cut costs by ramping up the speed of infrastructure and energy projects.
In a 62 to 33 vote, the upper chamber passed the measure on a bipartisan basis. The bill now heads to the House. President Trump has expressed support for the deal.

The vote follows years of on-and-off negotiations over how to speed up major infrastructure projects by streamlining the complicated permitting processes that can snag projects for years — an issue that has drawn more attention amid rising energy prices.
"This bill is years in the making," Senate Majority Leader John Thune said Thursday.

Supporters say the Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act, or BAAJA, will make it easier to build both renewable energy and fossil fuel projects, along with the high-tension power lines that support them. Negotiators announced a breakthrough on the legislation in September, touting a "historic, bipartisan agreement to reform America's federal environmental review and permitting processes."

"This is a major step toward making it faster and more efficient and easier to build infrastructure projects, certainly without giving up any of the strong protections for our environment," Republican Sen. Shelley Moore Capito of West Virginia said at the time.

Capito said the agreement represented "something that's become increasingly rare in Washington — Republicans and Democrats, sitting down, identifying a problem, and in this case a problem that has festered for at least a decade and more that impacts all Americans, and for us to sit down and work together to solve it." She said the American people "sent us here to do big things."
"This is a big thing," Capito said. "It's monumental, and it's legacy-setting."

GOP Sen. John Barrasso of Wyoming, who worked alongside Capito on permitting reform efforts for years, stressed the need for the legislation in a floor speech this week, saying, "If we want life to be more affordable in America, we need to make it more affordable to build in America, but also more convenient — more efficient."

The Wyoming Republican said, "In America today, it takes too long, and it costs too much to build," putting the blame on Washington for slowing things down, as projects are put in the "regulatory penalty box — waiting to act, waiting to build, workers sitting on the sidelines."

Barrasso lauded the bill for streamlining environmental and judicial reviews and limiting lawsuits, calling them common-sense reforms. He argued that the legislation represented a "responsible path" for producing more energy and protecting the environment, saying, "We can do both."

But some progressives have balked at the legislation, arguing it could erode environmental protections and doubting Mr. Trump will allow renewable projects to be built. While the bill does have the backing of some renewable energy leaders and developers, it also faced opposition from environmental groups.

Democratic Sen. Jeff Merkley of Oregon cited concerns about how it will affect states' rights to protect clean water and air, its implications for fossil fuel over renewable energy sources and how it could make it easier to build and power new data centers, along with its impact on the deficit. Sen. Ron Wyden, also of Oregon, opposed the bill as well, and sought a vote on an amendment to ban data centers on public lands.
The two senators have also expressed concern about how the bill could impact tribal rights.
"Embedded in this bill is a fundamental question about the direction we go regarding our responsibilities to this planet," Merkley said ahead of the vote Thursday.

Merkley acknowledged the bill could "turn the faucet potentially on" for renewable energy, but he said he's concerned Mr. Trump will continue to block wind energy projects. He argued that by allowing more natural gas and other fossil fuel projects, it will "open another floodgate for carbon that we won't ever be able to reverse."

After its passage in the Senate, the bill faces an uncertain future in the House, where opposition on multiple fronts has thrown into question whether the bill can make it through the lower chamber before year's end.

While some House Republicans have cited changes to the bill's provisions on transmission related to grid reliability, some House Democrats have also stressed that they would like to see the legislation altered. Rep. Jared Huffman of California, the ranking member on the House Natural Resources Committee, has raised doubts about the bill . In one all-caps X post , he argued the Trump administration could use the bill to approve fossil fuel projects while continuing to slow-walk renewable energy projects.
A spokesperson for House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries said earlier this month that he "supports the need for permitting reform," but argued the Senate's legislation "falls short in several areas."

"Leader Jeffries will not rubber-stamp legislation that emerges from the Senate without more constructive involvement with our caucus as we fight to make life more affordable for the American people," the spokesperson said.
body_zh: 华盛顿——周四，参议院批准了一项期待已久的两党许可改革法案，此前该法案在旨在通过加快基础设施和能源项目速度来削减成本的立法方面取得了重大突破。
上议院以 62 比 33 的投票结果在两党基础上通过了这项措施。该法案现在提交众议院。特朗普总统表达了对该协议的支持。
这次投票是在多年来断断续续的谈判之后进行的，谈判的主题是如何通过简化可能阻碍项目多年的复杂许可程序来加快重大基础设施项目的进程——在能源价格上涨的背景下，这一问题引起了更多关注。
“这项法案已经酝酿多年，”参议院多数党领袖约翰·图恩周四表示。
支持者表示，两党《美国负担能力和就业法案》（BAAJA）将使建设可再生能源和化石燃料项目以及支持这些项目的高压电线变得更加容易。谈判代表九月份宣布在立法上取得突破，并宣扬一项“改革美国联邦环境审查和许可程序的历史性两党协议”。
西弗吉尼亚州共和党参议员雪莱·摩尔·卡皮托当时表示：“这是朝着更快、更高效、更容易建设基础设施项目迈出的重要一步，当然不会放弃对我们环境的任何强有力的保护。”
卡皮托表示，该协议代表了“华盛顿越来越罕见的事情——共和党人和民主党人坐下来，找出一个问题，在这种情况下，这个问题已经恶化了至少十年以上，影响到所有美国人，需要我们坐下来共同努力解决它。”她说，美国人民“派我们来这里是为了做大事”。
“这是一件大事，”卡皮托说。 “这是具有纪念意义的，也是遗产设定。”
怀俄明州共和党参议员约翰·巴拉索(John Barrasso)多年来与卡皮托一起致力于允许改革工作，他在本周的一次发言中强调了立法的必要性，他说：“如果我们希望美国的生活变得更便宜，我们就需要让美国的建筑更便宜，而且更方便、更高效。”
这位怀俄明州共和党人表示，“在今天的美国，建设时间太长，建设成本太高”，他将责任归咎于华盛顿放慢了进程，因为项目被置于“监管惩罚箱中——等待采取行动，等待建设，工人们坐在场边”。
巴拉索称赞该法案简化了环境和司法审查并限制了诉讼，称其为常识性改革。他认为该立法代表了生产更多能源和保护环境的“负责任的道路”，并表示“我们可以两者兼得”。
但一些进步人士对这项立法犹豫不决，认为这可能会削弱环境保护，并怀疑特朗普是否会允许建设可再生能源项目。尽管该法案确实得到了一些可再生能源领导者和开发商的支持，但它也面临着环保组织的反对。
俄勒冈州民主党参议员杰夫·默克利(Jeff Merkley)表示担心它将如何影响各州保护清洁水和空气的权利、它对化石燃料相对于可再生能源的影响、它如何使新数据中心的建设和供电变得更容易，以及它对赤字的影响。同样来自俄勒冈州的参议员罗恩·怀登也反对该法案，并寻求对一项禁止公共土地上数据中心的修正案进行投票。
两位参议员还对该法案如何影响部落权利表示担忧。
默克利在周四投票前表示：“这项法案中包含一个基本问题，即我们对这个星球的责任的方向。”
默克利承认，该法案可能会“潜在地打开”可再生能源的水龙头，但他表示，他担心特朗普将继续阻止风能项目。他认为，通过允许更多的天然气和其他化石燃料项目，这将“打开另一扇我们永远无法逆转的碳闸门”。
在参议院通过后，该法案在众议院面临着不确定的未来，众议院多方面的反对对该法案能否在年底前在众议院获得通过提出了质疑。
虽然一些众议院共和党人提到了该法案中与电网可靠性相关的输电条款的变化，但一些众议院民主党人也强调，他们希望看到立法发生变化。众议院自然资源委员会资深成员、加利福尼亚州众议员贾里德·霍夫曼对该法案提出了质疑。在一篇全大写的 X 帖子中，他认为特朗普政府可以利用该法案批准化石燃料项目，同时继续缓慢推进可再生能源项目。
众议院少数党领袖哈基姆·杰弗里斯的发言人本月早些时候表示，他“支持允许改革的必要性”，但认为参议院的立法“在几个领域存在不足”。
这位发言人表示：“在我们努力让美国人民的生活变得更加负担得起的过程中，如果我们没有更多建设性地参与我们的党团会议，领导人杰弗里斯不会对参议院提出的立法盖上橡皮图章。”

title_en: Fiona the hippo dies after ingesting knitted hat at Cincinnati zoo
title_zh: 辛辛那提动物园河马菲奥娜误食针织帽后死亡
summary: Zoo staff tried a colonoscopy, vibration plate and other procedures to aid the hippo in passing the hat to no avail Fiona the hippo, one of America’s most famous zoo animals, has died after efforts to remove a knitted hat that she swallowed after it fell into
summary_zh: 动物园工作人员尝试了结肠镜检查、振动板和其他程序来帮助河马传递帽子，但无济于事。
body_en: Zoo staff tried a colonoscopy, vibration plate and other procedures to aid the hippo in passing the hat to no avail
Fiona the hippo, one of America’s most famous zoo animals, has died after efforts to remove a knitted hat that she swallowed after it fell into her enclosure proved unsuccessful.

“It is with extreme sadness that we share with you the devastating news that Fiona did not make it after multiple attempts from our amazing vets and keeper team to help her through what ended up being a medical emergency,” the zoo wrote in a post on social media .
With surgery too risky for full-grown hippos such as Fiona, who weighed in the region of 2,500lb (1,113kg), veterinarians tried an alternative method of getting the hat to pass through her system.

The hat fell near Fiona when a visitor to the Cincinnati zoo tossed it in the air, after which it bounced off a ceiling fan and fell into the enclosure, according to the Associated Press . Fiona ate the hat and was initially asymptomatic.
Fiona the hippo under veterinary care after eating hat at Cincinnati zoo
Days later, however, she began to lose appetite and staff at the zoo were forced to feed Fiona more in the hope that she would eventually get the hat through her digestive system.

“Despite multiple attempts to move the hat out of her system, it was ultimately too much to overcome. The team performed necessary supportive care today in an attempt to save her, but it was not successful and she did not recover,” the zoo statement said.
The zoo announced on Wednesday that the animal care team was using a vibration plate from a horse farm to help move things along, according to the Associated Press .

Fiona was sedated a second time on Tuesday for evaluation. After an ultrasound, veterinarians could see her intestines still trying to push the hat through. They also used a 9ft scope colonoscopy to view her intestines.

“The hope is that the vibrations will help encourage movement through her digestive tract and help the object pass,” the zoo had said on social media . Fiona remained out of her enclosure while she was receiving treatment.
Footage from the procedure released by the zoo on Wednesday shows her snorting and moving around her enclosure, which vets said was a sign of progress. Her hydration levels were being monitored.
Within an hour of the announcement, visitors began leaving flowers and cards by a hippo statue outside the zoo. “Forever our Fiona,” one note read.
Fiona became a global sensation after her premature birth in 2017, when she couldn’t stand on her own.

Fiona was born six weeks premature at just 29lb (13.2kgs), falling below the lowest recorded birth weight for her species at the time. Because she was initially too weak to nurse, Cincinnati Zoo staff hand-milked her mother while documenting Fiona’s recovery through photos and videos that captivated the internet.

Fiona admirers flocked to the zoo when her death was announced. Amy Haacke, a special educator from Dayton, said outside the Cincinnati Zoo that she has been a “huge fan” of Fiona since she was born because she likes underdogs. Haacke said she uses the Fiona book series in her classroom and owns three Fiona shirts.
“We were coming here anyway, but it kind of means a lot to be here,” Haacke said on Thursday. “We were here when she was first born and, I guess, now we’re here when she’s gone.”

Aftab Pureval, the Cincinnati mayor, said on social media that Fiona was “a symbol of perseverance and joy” in the city. Mike DeWine, the governor of Ohio, called her “a true icon”. The Cincinnati Bengals also expressed condolences , dubbing Fiona “the queen of the Queen City”.
The Cincinnati Reds baseball team also paid tribute : “Forever an icon. Rest in peace, Fiona.”
body_zh: 动物园工作人员尝试了结肠镜检查、振动板和其他程序来帮助河马传递帽子，但无济于事
河马菲奥娜是美国最著名的动物园动物之一，她在试图取出一顶掉进围栏后吞下的针织帽但没有成功后死亡。
动物园在社交媒体上的一篇帖子中写道：“我们非常悲伤地与大家分享这个毁灭性的消息，在我们出色的兽医和饲养员团队多次尝试帮助菲奥娜度过最终的医疗紧急情况后，菲奥娜最终还是没能成功。”
对于像菲奥娜这样体重约 2,500 磅（1,113 公斤）的成年河马来说，手术风险太大，兽医尝试了另一种方法，让帽子通过她的系统。
据美联社报道，辛辛那提动物园的一名游客将帽子抛向空中，帽子从吊扇上弹起，落入围栏内，掉落在菲奥娜附近。菲奥娜吃了帽子，最初没有任何症状。
辛辛那提动物园的河马菲奥娜在吃了帽子后正在接受兽医护理
然而几天后，她开始失去食欲，动物园的工作人员被迫给菲奥娜喂更多食物，希望她最终能通过消化系统得到帽子。
动物园声明称：“尽管多次尝试将帽子移出她的系统，但最终还是难以克服。今天，团队进行了必要的支持性护理，试图拯救她，但没有成功，她也没有康复。”
据美联社报道，动物园周三宣布，动物护理团队正在使用来自马场的振动板来帮助移动物体。
周二，菲奥娜第二次接受镇静剂评估。经过超声波检查后，兽医可以看到她的肠道仍在试图将帽子推过去。他们还使用 9 英尺镜结肠镜检查她的肠道。
动物园在社交媒体上表示：“希望振动能有助于促进它通过消化道的运动，并帮助物体通过。”菲奥娜在接受治疗期间一直留在围栏外。
动物园周三发布的手术视频显示，她在围栏内打喷嚏并四处走动，兽医称这是进展的迹象。她的水合水平正在接受监测。
消息公布后一个小时内，游客们开始在动物园外的河马雕像前留下鲜花和卡片。 “永远是我们的菲奥娜，”一张纸条上写着。
2017 年，菲奥娜 (Fiona) 早产，当时她无法独立站立，因此引起了全球轰动。
菲奥娜早产六周，体重仅为 29 磅（13.2 公斤），低于当时该物种的最低出生体重记录。由于菲奥娜最初太虚弱，无法哺乳，辛辛那提动物园的工作人员用手给她的母亲挤奶，同时通过在互联网上引起关注的照片和视频记录菲奥娜的康复情况。
Fiona admirers flocked to the zoo when her death was announced.来自代顿的特殊教育家艾米·哈克 (Amy Haacke) 在辛辛那提动物园外表示，自从菲奥娜出生以来，她一直是菲奥娜的“超级粉丝”，因为她喜欢弱者。哈克说，她在课堂上使用菲奥娜系列丛书，并拥有三件菲奥娜衬衫。
“无论如何我们都会来这里，但来到这里意义重大，”哈克周四说道。 “她刚出生时我们就在这里，我想，当她去世后我们就在这里。”
辛辛那提市市长阿夫塔布·普雷瓦尔在社交媒体上表示，菲奥娜是该市“毅力和欢乐的象征”。俄亥俄州州长迈克·德瓦恩 (Mike DeWine) 称她为“真正的偶像”。辛辛那提猛虎队也表达了哀悼，称菲奥娜为“皇后城女王”。
辛辛那提红人棒球队也表达了敬意：“永远的偶像。安息吧，菲奥娜。”

title_en: Iran may be working on biological weapons, Trump says
title_zh: 特朗普称伊朗可能正在研发生物武器
summary: President Trump told Fox News there are indications Iran may be working on biological or chemical weapons as the war drags on toward its ninth month.
summary_zh: 特朗普总统告诉福克斯新闻，有迹象表明，随着战争持续到第九个月，伊朗可能正在研究生物或化学武器。
body_en: President Trump told Fox News on Wednesday there are indications Iran may be working to develop biological or chemical weapons due to damage inflicted to its nuclear program, as tension in the nearly nine-month war appears to rise.

Iran claimed Thursday that two more oil tankers had hit sea mines in the Strait of Hormuz, causing fires on board. Iran's daily claims of vessels hitting mines have not been corroborated, but the United Arab Emirates' state oil company confirmed one crew member was missing Wednesday after one of its ships was struck by a projectile.
Bahrain and Kuwait said Wednesday they had intercepted weapons launched by Iran after the U.S. carried out strikes on Iran's Qeshm Island in the Strait of Hormuz.

The Saudi-led coalition fighting the Iran-backed Houthi militant group said it intercepted two drones toward Saudi Arabia's southern region.
The force's spokesperson, Turki al-Maliki, made the announcement in two separate social media posts . The coalition was not more specific about where in the south the drones had been intercepted.

3:03 PM / November 19, 2026 Trump's comments on chemical and biological weapons follow "same fraudulent script," Iranian official says

Iran's foreign ministry rejected President Trump's accusations the country is developing chemical or biological weapons and compared the situation to then-Secretary of State Colin Powell asserting Iraq had weapons of mass destruction.

"After the grand narrative of the 'Iranian nuclear threat,' U.S. officials are now claiming that there are indications Iran is developing biological or chemical weapons!" Iranian Foreign Ministry spokesperson Esmaeil Baqaei said in a post on X . "The allegations keep changing, but the underlying narrative remains disturbingly familiar. Once again, the world is apparently expected to suffer a bout of collective amnesia."
Baqaei raised the specter of the U.S. invasion of Iraq in 2003 over alleged development of weapons of mass destruction by Saddam Hussein's government and asked why Americans would fall for it again.

"Do American officials really expect the world to forget Colin Powell's infamous appearance before the U.N. Security Council in 2003, when he held up a small vial as a visual representation of the alleged threat posed by Iraq's weapons of mass destruction?" the spokesperson said. "That moment has since become an enduring symbol of one of the most consequential intelligence failures and political deceptions in modern history."
He added, "And now we find ourselves facing ominous new allegations and a narrative that appears to be following the same fraudulent script."

title_en: White House national cyber director leaving his post
title_zh: 白宫国家网络主管离职
summary: White House National Cyber Director Sean Cairncross will be leaving his position, a White House official told CBS News.
summary_zh: 一位白宫官员告诉哥伦比亚广播公司新闻，白宫国家网络主管肖恩·凯恩克罗斯将离职。
body_en: White House National Cyber Director Sean Cairncross will be leaving his position, a White House official told CBS News.
Cairncross was fired, multiple sources told CBS News.

White House chief of staff Stephen Miller — who took over for Susie Wiles earlier this month — had long wanted Cairncross out of the job, sources said, telling people he didn't think Cairncross had the expertise needed to be national cyber director.
Miller immediately teed up a search process for a replacement. Cairncross will be replaced by Kirsten Davies, who serves as the Pentagon's chief information officer, the sources said.
Axios was first to report that Cairncross will leave.

Cairncross' departure comes as the U.S. reels from a series of technological outages over the last week that have hit Microsoft services , air traffic control systems , banks and the National Security Agency's internal network .

Authorities investigating the outages have "seen nothing that would indicate that they are related," Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin told lawmakers this week. He said he is "98% confident" the outages are not the result of malicious foreign activity, though he acknowledged that he had "absolutely not" seen so many outages in a short period of time.

The national cyber director, a Senate-confirmed post, advises the president on cybersecurity and coordinates cyber strategy across the federal government . An attorney, Cairncross has served in the role since August 2025.
The job was created in 2021. In recent years, the U.S. has faced a series of cyberattacks linked to actors in Iran , Russia , China and other U.S. adversaries.

The Trump administration released its cyber strategy in March , which Cairncross' office oversaw. The seven-page document vowed to "detect, confront, and defeat cyber adversaries before they breach our networks and systems," harden critical infrastructure, maintain a U.S. edge in artificial intelligence and modernize federal tech systems.
In a November 2025 appearance at the Aspen Cyber Summit, Cairncross said one of the administration's primary goals is "introducing costs and consequences" on adversaries.

"I think, as a country, we have not done a terrific job of sending a signal to our adversaries that this behavior is not consequence-free," he said. "And we need to do that because it is scaling and it is becoming more aggressive every passing day."
If the Trump administration intends to nominate another permanent national cyber director, it only has a narrow window before the Senate changes to Democratic control in January.
In a statement, Cairncross called the role "the honor of a lifetime."

"I leave my role as Director of Cyber incredibly proud of our work to strengthen America's cybersecurity, protect our critical infrastructure, confront foreign threats, and position America to lead the world in Super Intelligence. None of it would have been possible without President Trump's extraordinary leadership," he said.

body_zh: 一位白宫官员告诉哥伦比亚广播公司新闻，白宫国家网络主管肖恩·凯恩克罗斯将离职。
多名消息人士告诉哥伦比亚广播公司新闻，凯恩克罗斯被解雇。
消息人士称，本月早些时候接替苏西·威尔斯的白宫办公厅主任斯蒂芬·米勒长期以来一直希望凯恩克罗斯辞职，并告诉人们，他认为凯恩克罗斯不具备担任国家网络主管所需的专业知识。
米勒立即启动了寻找替代者的工作。消息人士称，凯恩克罗斯将由五角大楼首席信息官克尔斯滕·戴维斯 (Kirsten Davies) 接替。
Axios 最先报道了凯恩克罗斯将离开的消息。
凯恩克罗斯离职之际，美国正遭受上周一系列技术故障的影响，这些故障影响了微软服务、空中交通管制系统、银行和国家安全局的内部网络。
国土安全部部长马克韦恩·穆林本周对立法者表示，调查此次停电的当局“没有发现任何迹象表明它们之间存在关联”。他表示，他“98%有信心”这次中断不是外国恶意活动造成的，不过他承认他“绝对没有”在短时间内看到如此多的中断。
国家网络总监是参议院确认的职位，负责向总统提供网络安全方面的建议，并协调整个联邦政府的网络战略。凯恩克罗斯 (Cairncross) 自 2025 年 8 月起担任律师。
该职位于 2021 年设立。近年来，美国面临一系列与伊朗、俄罗斯、中国和其他美国对手有关的网络攻击。
特朗普政府于三月份发布了网络战略，该战略由凯恩克罗斯办公室负责监督。这份长达七页的文件誓言要“在网络对手破坏我们的网络和系统之前发现、对抗和击败他们”，强化关键基础设施，保持美国在人工智能方面的优势，并使联邦技术系统现代化。
凯恩克罗斯在 2025 年 11 月出席阿斯彭网络峰会时表示，政府的主要目标之一是给对手“带来成本和后果”。
他说：“我认为，作为一个国家，我们没有向我们的对手发出信号，表明这种行为并非没有后果。” “我们需要这样做，因为它正在扩大规模，而且每天都变得更加激进。”
如果特朗普政府打算提名另一位常任国家网络主管，那么在参议院一月份将控制权转交给民主党之前，它的窗口期很短。
凯恩克罗斯在一份声明中称这个角色是“一生的荣幸”。
他说：“我在辞去网络主任一职时，对我们为加强美国网络安全、保护我们的关键基础设施、应对外国威胁以及使美国在超级情报领域引领世界所做的工作感到无比自豪。如果没有特朗普总统的非凡领导力，这一切都不可能实现。”

title_zh: 德克萨斯州对雷纳尔多·丹尼斯的处决失败，工作人员努力寻找静脉
summary: Dennes, 70, was convicted of killing a Houston jeweler, and groaned for an hour after pentobarbital was administered Texas executed Reinaldo Dennes on Thursday in a procedure that took over an hour as prison staffers struggled to find a suitable vein for the t
summary_zh: 70 岁的丹尼斯因杀害休斯敦的一名珠宝商而被定罪，在注射戊巴比妥后，他痛苦地呻吟了一小时。
body_en: Dennes, 70, was convicted of killing a Houston jeweler, and groaned for an hour after pentobarbital was administered

Texas executed Reinaldo Dennes on Thursday in a procedure that took over an hour as prison staffers struggled to find a suitable vein for the two intravenous needles carrying a lethal dose of pentobarbital, a sedative.

Dennes, who was found guilty of capital murder in the death of Janos Szucs, a diamond dealer found shot multiple times in his Houston office in January 1996, was the second person put to death in the US on Thursday, after Florida carried out a record-breaking 20th execution of the year, of Thomas Mitchell Overton.
Dennes gave a brief statement before the procedure began, then he told the warden: “Go, warden!”
Almost immediately he exclaimed over the pain, swearing and begging “the father” to “let me go”. He complained of more pain in his leg
then said, “I don’t think this is normal. Take me, father. Don’t let me suffer like this. C’mon.”

The procedure was completed at 7.07pm, 63 minutes after he was strapped to the gurney. A minute later, after being examined by a physician, Dennes was pronounced dead at 7.08pm at the penitentiary in Huntsville.
Prison officials said all procedures were followed appropriately.
This took place at the same time Florida carried out a record-breaking 20th execution for the year, of a man convicted of killing a pregnant woman and her husband during a home invasion.

Thomas Mitchell Overton, 71, was pronounced dead at 6.19pm after receiving a three-drug injection at Florida state prison in Raiford. In a final statement, he denied ever breaking into the couple’s home and attacking them, saying: “I never killed anyone.”
The executions of the two septuagenarians in one day reflect the ageing of the US death row population.

Overton was convicted of killing Michael and Susan MacIvor and their unborn child during an August 1991 break-in at their Florida Keys home. Dennes was convicted of capital murder in the death of Janos Szucs, a diamond dealer found shot multiple times in his office in January 1996.

On Thursday, Overton woke up at 5am and remained compliant, a Florida department of corrections spokesperson, Jordan Kirkland, said during a news conference. He did not meet with any visitors or a spiritual adviser.

Florida has now carried out more than half the country’s 39 executions this year under Ron DeSantis, the state’s outgoing Republican governor who has made aggressive use of the death penalty like few other governors. Thursday’s executions come amid renewed scrutiny of capital punishment in the US after Tennessee’s failed execution of Christa Pike in October.
Texas set a record for executions there when 40 people were put to death in 2000. Dennes became the ninth person to be executed by the state this year.

The execution followed renewed scrutiny of capital punishment in the US in the aftermath of Tennessee’s failed execution in September of Christa Pike, who survived two doses of pentobarbital that her lawyers say probably did not enter her bloodstream correctly and instead pooled in her arms, leaving them burned and blistered.
On Thursday, the US supreme court denied a final appeal in the Florida case while an appeal remained pending in the Texas case.
Overton was convicted in 1999 of two counts of first-degree murder and received a death sentence for each. Defense attorneys had argued that investigators had planted the DNA evidence.

The MacIvors were found dead in their Tavernier, Florida, home in August 1991, according to court records. Autopsies determined both were strangled and that Susan MacIvor, who was eight months pregnant, had been raped. Overton, who had worked at a gas station near the MacIvors’ home, was arrested on an unrelated burglary charge in 1996. Authorities said a sample taken from him matched the sample collected at the MacIvors’ home, and he was charged with their killings.
body_zh: 70 岁的丹尼斯因杀害休斯顿一名珠宝商而被定罪，在注射戊巴比妥后呻吟了一小时
德克萨斯州于周四处决了雷纳尔多·丹尼斯，整个过程持续了一个多小时，监狱工作人员努力为两根装有致命剂量的镇静剂戊巴比妥的静脉注射针找到合适的静脉。
丹尼斯因 1996 年 1 月钻石交易商亚诺什·苏克斯 (Janos Szucs) 的死亡而被判犯有死刑罪，丹尼斯是周四在佛罗里达州破纪录地执行了今年第 20 起托马斯·米切尔·奥弗顿 (Thomas Mitchell Overton) 处决事件后，美国第二个被处决的人。
丹尼斯在手术开始前发表了简短的声明，然后他告诉典狱长：“去吧，典狱长！”
几乎立刻，他就因疼痛而大声喊叫，咒骂并恳求“父亲”“放我走”。他抱怨腿部更加疼痛
然后说：“我觉得这不正常。带上我吧，父亲。不要让我这样受苦。来吧。”
手术于晚上 7 点 07 分完成，即他被绑在轮床上 63 分钟后。一分钟后，经过医生检查，丹尼斯于晚上 7 点 08 分在亨茨维尔监狱被宣布死亡。
监狱官员表示，所有程序均得到适当遵守。
与此同时，佛罗里达州破纪录地执行了今年第 20 起处决，一名男子因入室盗窃杀害一名孕妇及其丈夫而被定罪。
71 岁的托马斯·米切尔·奥弗顿 (Thomas Mitchell Overton) 于下午 6 点 19 分在位于赖福德的佛罗里达州监狱接受三种药物注射后被宣布死亡。在最后的声明中，他否认曾闯入这对夫妇的家并袭击他们，并说：“我从未杀过任何人。”
两名七十多岁老人一天内被处决，反映出美国死囚人口的老龄化。
奥弗顿因 1991 年 8 月闯入迈克尔和苏珊·麦基弗位于佛罗里达群岛的家中杀害了他们以及他们未出生的孩子而被定罪。 1996 年 1 月，一名钻石经销商杰诺斯·舒克斯 (Janos Szucs) 被发现在他的办公室内遭到多处枪杀，丹尼斯因此被判犯有死刑谋杀罪。
佛罗里达州惩教部门发言人乔丹·柯克兰 (Jordan Kirkland) 在新闻发布会上表示，周四，奥弗顿于凌晨 5 点醒来，并仍然遵守规定。他没有会见任何访客或精神顾问。
佛罗里达州在即将卸任的共和党州长罗恩·德桑蒂斯 (Ron DeSantis) 的领导下，已执行了今年全国 39 起死刑的一半以上，他像其他州长一样积极使用死刑。田纳西州十月份处决克里斯塔·派克失败后，美国对死刑重新进行了审查。
2000年，得克萨斯州处决了40人，创下了该州处决的纪录。丹尼斯成为今年该州第九个被处决的人。
田纳西州9月处决克里斯塔·派克(Christa Pike)失败后，美国对死刑重新进行了重新审查。克里斯塔·派克(Christa Pike)在注射了两剂戊巴比妥后幸存下来，她的律师称，戊巴比妥可能没有正确进入她的血液，而是聚集在她的手臂上，导致手臂烧伤和起泡。
周四，美国最高法院驳回了佛罗里达州案件的最终上诉，而德克萨斯州案件的上诉仍悬而未决。
1999年，奥弗顿被判犯有两项一级谋杀罪，每项均被判处死刑。辩护律师辩称，调查人员已经植入了 DNA 证据。
根据法庭记录，1991 年 8 月，麦基弗夫妇被发现死在佛罗里达州塔维尼尔的家中。尸检确定两人均被勒死，怀孕八个月的苏珊·麦基弗被强奸。奥弗顿曾在麦基弗家附近的一家加油站工作，1996 年因一项无关的入室盗窃罪被捕。当局称，从他身上采集的样本与在麦基弗家中采集的样本相符，因此他被指控犯有杀人罪。

title_en: US army postpones plan to detonate bomb-making chemical amid outcry
title_zh: 在强烈抗议下，美国陆军推迟了引爆炸弹化学物质的计划
summary: The controlled detonation can lead to a plume containing lead particles, worrying residents and state officials The US army has delayed its plan to detonate a stash of bomb-making chemicals in south-eastern Iowa as questions swirl about the public health risks
summary_zh: 受控爆炸可能会产生含有铅颗粒的羽流，令居民和州官员担忧美国陆军推迟了拆除计划
body_en: The controlled detonation can lead to a plume containing lead particles, worrying residents and state officials
The US army has delayed its plan to detonate a stash of bomb-making chemicals in south-eastern Iowa as questions swirl about the public health risks.
The army was set to blow up about 5 tons of lead azide in Middletown, Iowa , at noon on Friday, a move it described as the safest way to dispose of the highly sensitive compound.
During the controlled explosion, barrels of the material would be stored inside concrete structures and surrounded by sand-filled Hesco barriers reaching up two stories high.

Army officials advised certain residents of Middletown to evacuate between 8am and 2pm local time, due to the potential for window damage. The vibrations from the two blasts would not last long but could break old windows in town, and the resulting dust was expected to linger for no more than one hour, depending on wind speed, officials said.
The detonation is also expected to produce a plume containing lead particles.

Officials have released maps showing the potential for lead dust to drift north. Updated maps showed the plume’s shift, and the army will continue to update the map based on weather. Some schools in the path of the plume have already canceled classes.
Nearly 400 people live in Middletown, but there are thousands more in the path of the plume.
While the army recommends cleaning cars, windowsills and outdoor surfaces after the detonation, residents have taken to social media to voice concern and question whether that will be enough.
Iowa’s top leaders appeared to learn about the plan along with the public. The office of the Iowa governor, Kim Reynolds, was first briefed on Monday about the public advisory, her office said.

“An unacceptable lack of communication and clarity has made Iowans understandably concerned and angry about this situation,” governor-elect Rob Sand wrote on X on Thursday. “The public deserves to know, if this is the safest option, why other options were worse.”
Adam Telle, the acting secretary of the US army, alluded to the criticism in his Thursday announcement about the delayed detonation.
“Public communication is essential to public trust,” he wrote on X, adding that he was engaging state officials.
The plan is now expected to proceed on Monday. According to Telle, it’s the “latest possible moment”, before temperatures drop, which could risk destabilizing the material.
Babies more likely to have heart defects from Louisiana’s areas with industrial pollution, study finds

Middletown residents learned in March that the army needed to dispose of several dozen barrels containing lead azide, after the ammunition plant paused operations as part of a review and the degraded material was discovered.

“The safety of our people and our neighbors is non‑negotiable,” Lt Col Daniel Nosse, the commander of the plant, said at the time, acknowledging the volatility of the chemical compound used in munitions production.

The army shared more details during a public meeting in Middletown in October, advising that a detonation was planned for an unspecified date in November. The Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) on 13 November approved an emergency permit, paving the way for Friday’s detonation.

That permit required the army to track specific rates of potential air and dust dispersion and notify the public five days in advance, prompting Sunday’s original advisory to communities as far as 100 miles (160km) away.
body_zh: 受控爆炸可能会产生含有铅颗粒的羽流，令居民和州官员感到担忧
由于公众对公共卫生风险的质疑不断，美国陆军推迟了在爱荷华州东南部引爆一批制造炸弹的化学品的计划。
军队定于周五中午在爱荷华州米德尔敦炸毁约 5 吨叠氮化铅，军方称此举是处理高度敏感化合物的最安全方法。
在受控爆炸期间，成桶的材料将储存在混凝土结构内，周围是两层楼高的填满沙子的 Hesco 屏障。
陆军官员建议米德尔敦的某些居民在当地时间上午 8 点至下午 2 点之间撤离，因为窗户可能会损坏。官员们表示，两次爆炸产生的震动不会持续很长时间，但可能会打破镇上的旧窗户，而由此产生的灰尘预计不会超过一小时，具体时间取决于风速。
爆炸预计还会产生含有铅颗粒的羽流。
官员们发布的地图显示铅尘有可能向北漂移。更新的地图显示了羽流的变化，军队将继续根据天气更新地图。羽流路径上的一些学校已经停课。
米德尔敦有近 400 人居住，但羽流路径上还有数千人。
虽然军队建议在爆炸后清洁汽车、窗台和室外表面，但居民们在社交媒体上表达了担忧，并质疑这是否足够。
爱荷华州的最高领导人似乎与公众一起了解了该计划。爱荷华州州长金·雷诺兹 (Kim Reynolds) 的办公室表示，她的办公室于周一首次听取了有关公共咨询的简报。
当选州长罗布·桑德 (Rob Sand) 周四在 X 上写道：“沟通和清晰度的缺乏令人无法接受，这让爱荷华州人对这种情况感到担忧和愤怒，这是可以理解的。” “公众应该知道，如果这是最安全的选择，为什么其他选择更糟糕。”
美国陆军代理部长亚当·泰尔在周四的声明中提到了对延迟爆炸的批评。
“公共沟通对于公众信任至关重要，”他在 X 上写道，并补充说他正在与州官员接触。
该计划目前预计将于周一进行。泰勒表示，这是“最后可能的时刻”，在温度下降之前，温度可能会破坏材料的稳定性。
研究发现路易斯安那州工业污染地区的婴儿更容易患有心脏缺陷
米德尔敦居民三月份获悉，在弹药厂因审查而暂停运营并发现了降解材料后，军队需要处理数十个含有叠氮化铅的桶。
该工厂指挥官丹尼尔·诺斯中校当时表示：“我们人民和邻居的安全是不容谈判的。”他承认用于弹药生产的化合物具有挥发性。
10 月，军方在米德尔敦举行的一次公开会议上分享了更多细节，并表示计划在 11 月的某个具体日期进行爆炸。美国环境保护局 (EPA) 于 11 月 13 日批准了紧急许可证，为周五的爆炸铺平了道路。
该许可证要求军队跟踪潜在空气和灰尘扩散的具体速度，并提前五天通知公众，这促使周日向远至 100 英里（160 公里）外的社区发出最初的建议。

body_en: Gregory Meeks raises concerns about Trump, Xi and Putin summit : NPR

Gregory Meeks raises concerns about Trump, Xi and Putin summit Rep. Gregory Meeks raises concerns about U.S. alliances after Trump's summit with Xi and Putin. He also discusses Chinese espionage amid the Nvidia scandal.
Rep. Gregory Meeks, D-N.Y., on Trump's meeting with Chinese President Xi Jinping
Rep. Gregory Meeks, D-N.Y., speaks to reporters outside a House Democratic Caucus meeting at the Longworth House Office Building in Washington on Nov. 10. Aaron Schwartz/Getty Images hide caption
Trump, Xi and Putin meet as global alliances hang in the balance

Rep. Gregory Meeks, the top Democrat on the House Foreign Affairs Committee, questioned Thursday what President Trump accomplished in his summit with the leaders of China and Russia, warning that the meeting could undermine U.S. alliances.
"I wish he had a plan and a strategy if he was going to meet with them and goals. Apparently, he does not," Meeks told Morning Edition.

His comments followed Trump's meeting with Chinese President Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin in Shenzhen, China, which ended with few signs of progress on nuclear arms control or the war in Ukraine.

Meeks said he feared the leaders were discussing dividing the world into spheres of influence, potentially sidelining U.S. allies. He also questioned the lack of meaningful agreements on nuclear weapons and artificial intelligence safety.
Asked about the Nvidia scandal, Meeks said he would confront Xi over Chinese espionage and intellectual property theft and warn of possible retaliation.
"When it comes to our national security, that's where we draw a red line," he said.

Meeks argued that U.S. diplomats should have raised concerns about Chinese espionage and intellectual property theft before the summit to establish clear goals for the talks. In his conversation with NPR's A Martínez, Meeks also called for reducing tariffs on U.S. allies while pressing China to end its support for Russia's war in Ukraine.
