summary: A federal judge ruled that messages sent by Brooke Rollins to USDA workers suggest Christianity is a shared faith and violate the first amendment Religious messages that US agriculture secretary Brooke Rollins emailed to the agency’s 100,000 employees were unc
summary_zh: 一名联邦法官裁定，布鲁克·罗林斯向美国农业部工作人员发送的信息表明基督教是一种共同的信仰，违反了《宪法第一修正案》
body_en: A federal judge ruled that messages sent by Brooke Rollins to USDA workers suggest Christianity is a shared faith and violate the first amendment

Religious messages that US agriculture secretary Brooke Rollins emailed to the agency’s 100,000 employees were unconstitutional, and she must be careful to avoid proselytizing when communicating with workers, a federal judge ruled Thursday.

Rollins sent the messages, which included Christian messages and images, from her official email account on holidays such as Independence Day, Thanksgiving, Christmas and Easter. She did not send messages commemorating holidays from other religions.

“And so, like the very first disciples to encounter our risen Lord in the Upper Room almost two thousand years ago, this Easter let us too be alive with hope, full of Paschal joy, and confident in the mission each of us has been called for,” Rollins wrote in a 5 April email, marking Easter.

US district judge Trina Thompson in San Francisco said the emails violated the first amendment’s establishment clause, pointing to her position of authority, her use of an official email account and the messages suggesting that Christianity is the shared faith of Department of Agriculture (USDA) workers.
The USDA did not respond to a request for comment.

Employees cannot realistically opt out of reading emails from their agency director, and the messages could coerce them to hide their own faith or feel pressure to adopt Rollins’ Christian faith, Thompson ruled.

When disseminating religious messages, Rollins must stop if a colleague asks her to. “Cannot create a hostile work environment through persistent unwelcome advances” and “cannot use official authority to pressure subordinates” are commands that were quoted directly from a USDA policy on workplace religious expression that Rollins herself adopted.

Rollins may discuss her faith with interested colleagues, share why her faith is meaningful to her, politely invite co-workers to religious events and express her views in appropriate conversations, Thompson ruled, again quoting directly from Rollins’ policy.
Six USDA employees and the National Federation of Federal Employees, a labor union representing 19,000 USDA workers, brought the suit in May.
body_zh: 一名联邦法官裁定，布鲁克·罗林斯向美国农业部工作人员发送的信息表明基督教是一种共同的信仰，违反了第一修正案
一位联邦法官周四裁定，美国农业部长布鲁克·罗林斯通过电子邮件向该机构的 10 万名员工发送的宗教信息违反宪法，她在与工人沟通时必须小心避免传教。
罗林斯在独立日、感恩节、圣诞节和复活节等假期从她的官方电子邮件帐户发送这些信息，其中包括基督教信息和图像。她没有发送纪念其他宗教节日的信息。
罗林斯在 4 月 5 日纪念复活节的电子邮件中写道：“因此，就像大约两千多年前在晚餐厅遇到我们复活的主的第一批门徒一样，这个复活节也让我们充满希望，充满逾越节的喜乐，并对我们每个人所肩负的使命充满信心。”
美国旧金山地区法官特里娜·汤普森表示，这些电子邮件违反了第一修正案的确立条款，指出她的权威地位、她使用官方电子邮件帐户以及暗示基督教是农业部工作人员共同信仰的信息。
美国农业部没有回应置评请求。
汤普森裁定，员工实际上无法选择不阅读其机构主管的电子邮件，这些信息可能会迫使他们隐藏自己的信仰，或感受到接受罗林斯基督教信仰的压力。
在传播宗教信息时，如果同事要求，罗林斯必须停止。 “不能通过持续不受欢迎的行为创造一个充满敌意的工作环境”和“不能利用官方权威向下属施压”这些命令直接引用自美国农业部关于工作场所宗教表达的政策，罗林斯本人也采用了这一政策。
汤普森再次直接引用罗林斯的政策，裁定罗林斯可以与感兴趣的同事讨论她的信仰，分享为什么她的信仰对她有意义，礼貌地邀请同事参加宗教活动，并在适当的对话中表达她的观点。
六名美国农业部雇员和代表 19,000 名美国农业部工人的全国联邦雇员联合会于 5 月提起诉讼。

title_en: Trump, Xi and Putin meet as global alliances hang in the balance
title_zh: 特朗普、习近平和普京会面，全球联盟岌岌可危
summary: President Trump, China's Xi Jinping and Russia's Vladimir Putin have gathered in Shenzhen, China, for a historic trilateral meeting, with Ukraine, Iran and nuclear disarmament on the agenda.
summary_zh: 特朗普总统、中国国家主席习近平和俄罗斯总统弗拉基米尔·普京齐聚中国深圳，与乌克兰、伊朗伊斯兰共和国举行历史性三边会议
body_en: The world order in focus as Trump meets Xi and Putin : NPR

The world order in focus as Trump meets Xi and Putin President Trump, China's Xi Jinping and Russia's Vladimir Putin have gathered in Shenzhen, China, for a historic trilateral meeting, with Ukraine, Iran and nuclear disarmament on the agenda.

President Trump, right, Chinese President Xi Jinping, center, and Russian President Vladimir Putin arrive for a trilateral meeting at Kylin Villa in Shenzhen, China, on Thursday. Win McNamee/Pool photo via AP hide caption

SHENZHEN, China, and MOSCOW, Russia — President Trump joined Chinese President Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin for a trilateral summit in Shenzhen, China on Thursday. Their meeting capped two days of talks characterized by high-minded tributes to the role of great powers in maintaining peace, even though some of those powers had a role in starting some of the most intractable conflicts around the globe.
"History tells us when great powers are at peace, the world is secure," Xi said in opening remarks before cameras. "When great powers clash, the world is in chaos."
Putin noted their nations could make a "significant contribution to strengthening security and stability in the world."
"In that sense and I think in lots of other ways, we are making history," said Trump, who called it a "special responsibility" for the three countries to work together.
Trump heads to Asia to meet with Xi and Putin amid Nvidia fallout
Yet, they offered few solutions toward peace, with the leaders laying out divergent agendas going in

Trump wanted to talk about reducing nuclear weapons and his mission to keep Iran from obtaining them; Putin was looking to push for an end to the war in Ukraine on terms favorable to Moscow; Xi was signaling he hoped to avoid wading too deep into either topic — preferring to showcase China's growing global clout with more general statements promoting peace and economic stability.
There were also topics to avoid: Trump refused to engage with journalists' questions over China's alleged role in an espionage plot to smuggle in high-end Nvidia chips .

In the end, the summit's key deliverable was arguably the image itself: the president of the United States gathering with authoritarian leaders from China and Russia for the first time in American history.

Despite being billed as a summit of "groundbreaking significance" by the Chinese hosts, sit-down talks between Trump, Xi and Putin were relatively brief — with some of that time taken up by interpreters delivering simultaneous translation.
Trump's meeting with Putin lasted 42 minutes. His talks with Xi went about an hour. The trilateral group session went on for an hour and a half.
Still, it was enough time for familiar Trump bonhomie to emerge.
"Who's he? He's my friend," said a smiling Trump upon seeing Putin ahead of their bilateral meeting.
"We've known each other for a long time," Trump added after he and the Russian leader warmly shook hands. "And I think a lot of wonderful things can come of this. Or at least start."
Similarly, Trump told Xi "as long as you and I are in charge of things, we're never going to have a problem."
body_zh: 特朗普会见习近平和普京时，世界秩序成为焦点：NPR
特朗普会见习近平和普京，世界秩序成为焦点 特朗普总统、中国国家主席习近平和俄罗斯总统弗拉基米尔·普京齐聚中国深圳，举行历史性三边会议，议程包括乌克兰、伊朗和核裁军问题。
周四，特朗普总统（右）、中国国家主席习近平（中）和俄罗斯总统弗拉基米尔·普京抵达中国深圳麒麟山庄参加三边会议。通过美联社赢得 McNamee/Pool 照片 隐藏标题栏
中国深圳和俄罗斯莫斯科——周四，特朗普总统与中国国家主席习近平和俄罗斯总统普京在中国深圳举行三边峰会。他们的会议结束了为期两天的会谈，其特点是对大国在维护和平方面的作用表示崇高敬意，尽管其中一些大国在引发全球一些最棘手的冲突方面发挥了作用。
“历史告诉我们，大国和平，世界就安全，”习近平在镜头前致开幕词时说道。 “当大国发生冲突时，世界就会陷入混乱。”
普京指出，他们的国家可以“为加强世界安全与稳定做出重大贡献”。
特朗普说：“从这个意义上说，我认为从很多其他方面来说，我们正在创造历史。”他称这三个国家的合作是一项“特殊责任”。
在英伟达的影响下，特朗普前往亚洲会见习近平和普京
然而，他们没有提出什么和平解决方案，领导人制定了不同的议程。
特朗普想谈论削减核武器以及他阻止伊朗获得核武器的使命；普京希望以有利于莫斯科的条件推动结束乌克兰战争。习近平表示，他希望避免太深入地讨论这两个话题，而是更愿意通过促进和平与经济稳定的更笼统的声明来展示中国日益增长的全球影响力。
还有一些话题需要回避：特朗普拒绝回答记者有关中国涉嫌参与走私高端英伟达芯片间谍活动的问题。
最终，峰会的关键成果可以说是形象本身：美国总统在美国历史上首次与中国和俄罗斯的独裁领导人会面。
尽管中国东道主将峰会宣传为具有“开创性意义”的峰会，但特朗普、习近平和普京之间的坐下来会谈相对简短——其中一些时间是由口译员进行同声传译。
特朗普与普京的会面持续了42分钟。他与习近平的会谈持续了大约一个小时。三边小组会议持续了一个半小时。
尽管如此，这段时间已经足够让特朗普熟悉的友善态度显现出来了。
“他是谁？他是我的朋友，”特朗普在双边会晤前见到普京时微笑着说道。
“我们认识很久了，”特朗普在与俄罗斯领导人热情握手后补充道。 “我认为这会带来很多美好的事情。或者至少开始。”
同样，特朗普告诉习近平“只要你和我负责事情，我们就永远不会有问题。”

title_en: Beshear defends Texas strategy
title_zh: 贝希尔捍卫德克萨斯州战略
summary: The chair of the Democratic Governors Association has taken fire for not spending enough on Gov.-elect Gina Hinojosa’s race in Texas
summary_zh: 民主党州长协会主席因没有为德克萨斯州当选州长吉娜·伊诺霍萨的竞选投入足够的资金而受到批评
body_en: Kentucky Gov. Andy Beshear defended his decision not to invest more in Gina Hinojosa’s successful race for Texas governor in an interview with POLITICO, amid criticism that could derail his own potential presidential ambitions.

Beshear, the chair of the Democratic Governors Association, took heat this month when Latino Democratic operatives and Hinojosa allies publicly maligned him for failing to do enough to help Hinojosa over the finish line.
“There might have been frustration by folks who just really wanted to win that race, but they did, and she did, and we're very excited to have her a part of the DGA room,” Beshear said Thursday.
“Did we spend a little more money, say, in Kansas, where we were trying to protect the seat? Yes, but we only won that race by 7,000 votes," he said.

In a stunning victory, Hinojosa won Texas by 7 percentage points. Hinojosa’s allies’ say that their calls for the DGA to support her campaign went unanswered for months. Ultimately, the DGA contributed $1.4 million — a far cry from the $19 million the organization invested in Keisha Lance Bottoms’ successful bid to win Georgia’s governorship.
But Beshear said the context matters. When the budget for this campaign cycle started at the end of 2024, Democrats had suffered brutal losses.

“We built out our map protecting our incumbents,” Beshear said. “We were going to be lucky to get [Arizona Gov.] Katie Hobbs and [Oregon Gov.] Tina Kotek reelected, and we were going to have tough elections, even in places potentially like Pennsylvania.”

Democrats Abigail Spanberger in Virginia and Mikie Sherrill in New Jersey both won gubernatorial victories in 2025 on affordability platforms, which helped propel them to victory at a time when the economy had become a key pressure point for voters.

Heading into 2026, Beshear said, "what came online were the first set of flips, where the earliest polling indicated it was possible, and those were Iowa, Ohio, Georgia and Nevada. And so at that point, we already had the largest DGA map ever."

“We had a size 10 budget with a size 14 map, and then what happened? Alaska, Nebraska, Oklahoma, Texas and Florida all became or seemed competitive as well, which meant we had a size 10 budget with a size 16 map," Beshear said.
The party flipped six governorships in states that President Donald Trump won. In January, Democrats will control 30 governorships and the majority of state legislative chambers.
“So at the end of the day, I think we're judged by results,” Beshear said. “And I get that every campaign wants as much funding as they can, but Gina won in Texas, and I'm excited for her.”
While Beshear hasn’t publicly announced a run for president in 2028, he’s already crafting his pitch.

“If you look at what we've done in Kentucky, the ability to do that all across this country would be special for so many other communities that deserve better jobs, more accessible health care and a better life for our people,” he said.
Despite his role as chair of the DGA, Beshear argues that of all the rumored candidates out there, he would be the “ultimate outsider.” He’s not from “inside the Beltway” or either coast.
He would be “a candidate from where the South meets the Midwest,” he said — a governor who has helped “improve and revive a place that the country for many years left out.”
Beshear says that Bottoms’ victory in Georgia showed Democrats can win in the South.

“I am a Southern governor that has won in a red state, and so I knew a great candidate when I saw one,” he said. “And together, our financial support plus her grassroots campaign that turned out voters sent a message that the South is winnable and that the Deep South is winnable.”
Next up? Mississippi and Louisiana, Beshear said.

“You look at Mississippi, where three years ago the election was close and will be again,” he said. “And then, depending on the candidate we get in Louisiana, the governor there has incredibly low approval ratings, and so even though that's going up against an incumbent, I think the seat is very much in play.”
body_zh: 肯塔基州州长安迪·贝希尔在接受《政治》杂志采访时，为自己不为吉娜·伊诺霍萨成功竞选德克萨斯州州长进行更多投资的决定进行了辩护，因为批评可能会破坏他自己潜在的总统野心。
民主党州长协会主席贝希尔本月受到了批评，因为拉丁裔民主党成员和伊诺霍萨盟友公开诽谤他未能采取足够措施帮助伊诺霍萨冲过终点线。
贝希尔周四表示：“那些真正想赢得那场比赛的人可能会感到沮丧，但他们做到了，她也做到了，我们很高兴她能成为 DGA 会议室的一员。”
“我们是否花了更多的钱，比如说，在堪萨斯州，我们试图保护席位？是的，但我们只以 7,000 票赢得了那场比赛，”他说。
伊诺霍萨以惊人的胜利赢得德克萨斯州 7 个百分点。伊诺霍萨的盟友表示，他们要求 DGA 支持她的竞选活动的呼吁几个月来都没有得到回应。最终，DGA 捐赠了 140 万美元，与该组织为凯莎·兰斯·博顿斯 (Keisha Lance Bottoms) 成功竞选佐治亚州州长而投入的 1900 万美元相差甚远。
但贝希尔表示，背景很重要。当这个竞选周期的预算于 2024 年底开始时，民主党遭受了惨重的损失。
“我们制定了保护我们现任者的地图，”贝希尔说。 “我们将很幸运让[亚利桑那州州长]凯蒂·霍布斯和[俄勒冈州州长]蒂娜·科特克连任，我们将进行艰难的选举，即使是在宾夕法尼亚州等可能的地方。”
弗吉尼亚州的民主党人阿比盖尔·斯潘伯格和新泽西州的民主党人米基·谢里尔都凭借负担能力平台赢得了 2025 年州长选举的胜利，这帮助他们在经济成为选民的关键压力点之际取得了胜利。
进入 2026 年，Beshear 说，“上线的是第一组翻转，最早的民意调查表明这是可能的，这些翻转是爱荷华州、俄亥俄州、佐治亚州和内华达州。所以在那时，我们已经有了有史以来最大的 DGA 地图。”
“我们有 10 号的预算和 14 号的地图，然后发生了什么？阿拉斯加、内布拉斯加州、俄克拉荷马州、得克萨斯州和佛罗里达州都变得或看起来具有竞争力，这意味着我们有 10 号的预算和 16 号的地图，”Beshear 说。
该党在唐纳德·特朗普总统赢得的州中推翻了六个州长职位。一月份，民主党将控制 30 个州长职位和大多数州议会。
“所以归根结底，我认为我们是根据结果来评判的，”贝希尔说。 “我知道每个竞选活动都希望获得尽可能多的资金，但吉娜在德克萨斯州获胜，我为她感到兴奋。”
虽然贝希尔尚未公开宣布竞选 2028 年总统，但他已经在精心准备自己的竞选方案。
他说：“如果你看看我们在肯塔基州所做的事情，那么在全国范围内做到这些的能力对于许多其他社区来说将具有特殊意义，这些社区的人民理应享有更好的工作、更便捷的医疗保健和更美好的生活。”
尽管贝希尔担任 DGA 主席，但他认为，在所有传闻中的候选人中，他将是“最终的局外人”。他不是来自“环城公路内”或任何一个海岸。
他说，他将成为“来自南方与中西部交汇处的候选人”——一位帮助“改善和复兴这个国家多年来忽视的地方”的州长。
贝希尔说，巴托姆斯在佐治亚州的胜利表明民主党可以在南方获胜。
“我是一名南方州长，在一个红色州获胜，所以当我看到一个伟大的候选人时，我就知道了，”他说。 “我们的财政支持加上她的草根竞选活动向选民传达了一个信息：南方是可以获胜的，南方腹地是可以获胜的。”
接下来？ Mississippi and Louisiana, Beshear said.

“你看看密西西比州，三年前那里的选举结果很接近，而且还会再次发生，”他说。 “And then, depending on the candidate we get in Louisiana, the governor there has incredibly low approval ratings, and so even though that's going up against an incumbent, I think the seat is very much in play.”

title_en: Exclusive: Rep. Gregory Meeks vows to reclaim Congress' powers from Trump
title_zh: 独家：众议员格雷戈里·米克斯誓言从特朗普手中夺回国会权力
summary: Rep. Gregory Meeks (D-N.Y.) said Thursday Congress is going to reclaim powers long ceded to the executive branch at the Axios Future of Defense summit. Why it matters: As the top Democrat on the House Foreign Affairs Committee, Meeks is putting the Trump admin
summary_zh: 纽约州民主党众议员格雷戈里·米克斯周四表示，国会将收回在 Axios 国防未来峰会上长期割让给行政部门的权力
body_en: Rep. Gregory Meeks (D-N.Y.) said Thursday Congress is going to reclaim powers long ceded to the executive branch at the Axios Future of Defense summit.

Why it matters: As the top Democrat on the House Foreign Affairs Committee, Meeks is putting the Trump administration on notice that it's foreign policy decisions are going to be challenged through legislation and oversight hearings.
What they're saying: "Whether it's a Democratic president or Republican president, we've ceded too much and we've got to stand up and take it back," Meeks told Axios' Colin Demarest.
"We do, at times, have to make some difficult decisions, and not just punt them away to the executive branch, because when you do that, it's hard to get them back."
Meeks also suggested that incoming House Speaker Hakeem Jeffries (D-N.Y.) may be willing to take the Trump administration to court if needed to enforce congressional oversight.
"If it takes some litigation to do that, we will do that," Meeks said. "Speaker Johnson wouldn't do it. I think Speaker Jeffries will do it."
Catch up quick: Meeks will likely become Foreign Affairs committee chair in January, riding the blue wave that gave Democrats the ability to control Congress' legislative agenda.
Zoom in: Meeks didn't rule out calling Secretary of State Marco Rubio to testify before the committee.
"The jurisdiction of the House Foreign Affairs Committee is the State Department," Meeks said.

Later, he added more broadly, "[y]ou can run, but you can't hide... We're going to use the power that the committee and the Constitution gives us to make sure that we're calling in members of that administration, so they have to answer to the American people, why what has taken place has taken place."

Zoom out: Meeks has already sent document-preservation letters to seven agencies, including the State Department, USAID and the U.S. International Development Finance Corporation, warning them to avoid destroying records that could be relevant to oversight efforts.
He threatened the possibility of criminal referrals if someone is found to have done otherwise.
What we're watching: Meeks said Democrats plan to address affordability concerns and introduce another War Powers Resolution aimed at the Iran war.
He also floated litigation and using Congress' power of the purse, including withholding funds, as ways to force the Trump administration to comply.
"The people have spoken loudly and clearly that they are against the war in Iran," Meeks said. "They see how foreign policy directly now connects to domestic policy."
He added that Democrats need to investigate what's happening in the Middle East, and explain to Americans what's at stake in the war.
"That is the job, a part of the job, of the Foreign Affairs Committee, and that's exactly what we're going to do on day one."
Editor's note: This story has been updated with additional information throughout.
body_zh: 纽约州民主党众议员格雷戈里·米克斯周四表示，国会将收回在 Axios 国防未来峰会上长期割让给行政部门的权力。
为什么重要：作为众议院外交事务委员会的最高民主党人，米克斯提醒特朗普政府，其外交政策决定将通过立法和监督听证会受到挑战。
他们的说法是：“无论是民主党总统还是共和党总统，我们都放弃了太多，我们必须站起来夺回，”米克斯告诉 Axios 的科林·德马雷斯特 (Colin Demarest)。
“有时，我们确实必须做出一些艰难的决定，而不仅仅是把它们扔给行政部门，因为当你这样做时，很难让它们回来。”
米克斯还表示，如果需要加强国会监督，即将上任的众议院议长哈基姆·杰弗里斯（纽约州民主党）可能愿意将特朗普政府告上法庭。
“如果需要一些诉讼才能做到这一点，我们就会这么做，”米克斯说。 “约翰逊议长不会这么做。我认为杰弗里斯议长会这么做。”
快点赶上：米克斯很可能在一月份成为外交事务委员会主席，乘着蓝色浪潮，让民主党有能力控制国会的立法议程。
放大：米克斯不排除传唤国务卿马可·卢比奥在委员会作证。
“众议院外交事务委员会的管辖范围是国务院，”米克斯说。
后来，他更广泛地补充道，“你可以竞选，但你不能隐藏……我们将利用委员会和宪法赋予我们的权力，确保我们召集政府成员，所以他们必须向美国人民负责，为什么发生了这些事情。”
缩小范围：米克斯已经向包括国务院、美国国际开发署和美国国际开发金融公司在内的七个机构发出了文件保存信，警告他们避免销毁可能与监督工作相关的记录。
他威胁说，如果发现有人有其他行为，可能会被移送至刑事部门。
我们正在关注的内容：米克斯表示，民主党计划解决负担能力问题，并提出另一项针对伊朗战争的战争权力决议。
他还提出诉讼并利用国会的财政权力（包括扣留资金）来迫使特朗普政府遵守规定。
米克斯说：“人们大声而明确地表示，他们反对伊朗战争。” “他们看到外交政策现在如何与国内政策直接联系起来。”
他补充说，民主党需要调查中东正在发生的事情，并向美国人解释战争的利害关系。
“这就是外交事务委员会的工作，工作的一部分，而这正是我们第一天要做的事情。”

title_en: Appeals court rejects Democrat LaMonica McIver’s bid to toss charges over ICE protest
title_zh: 上诉法院驳回民主党拉莫尼卡·麦克莱弗 (LaMonica McIver) 提出的撤销对 ICE 抗议指控的请求
summary: New Jersey congresswoman, charged with interfering with immigration arrest, set to face trial over May 2025 incident An appeals court decided on Thursday that the Democratic New Jersey representative LaMonica McIver will continue to face charges related to a s
summary_zh: 新泽西州女议员被控干涉移民逮捕，将因 2025 年 5 月事件接受审判 上诉法院于周四做出裁决
body_en: Appeals court rejects Democrat LaMonica McIver’s bid to toss charges over ICE protest | ICE (US Immigration and Customs Enforcement)
New Jersey congresswoman, charged with interfering with immigration arrest, set to face trial over May 2025 incident

An appeals court decided on Thursday that the Democratic New Jersey representative LaMonica McIver will continue to face charges related to a skirmish outside an immigration detention center last year when she attempted to conduct an oversight visit there.

The court’s decision to decline McIver’s request to overturn the court’s earlier ruling comes just a day after she pressed the homeland security secretary for the Trump administration’s aggressive immigration enforcement operations, telling the secretary: “You are killing people.”
Now, with the court’s decision, she is facing a likely trial for the May 2025 incident.
ICE offers contractor operating deportation flights windfall and secrecy, data shows

“Because of a weaponized Department of Justice, and because I dared to do my job and conduct oversight of ICE, I am facing 17 years in prison,” McIver said in a statement on Thursday. “Now, due to the disappointing decision by the third circuit, we are all one step closer to a world in which the president of the United States can try to imprison people simply because he does not like what they stand for.”

McIver was charged last year with assaulting, resisting, impeding and interfering with federal officers. The prosecution led to a lengthy legal battle, with McIver claiming the prosecution represented a political attack by the Trump administration.

McIver has attempted to have the case dismissed on various grounds, including by arguing the constitution protects her from prosecution. The third circuit court of appeals rejected her arguments in August and on Thursday declined her request to have an “en banc” hearing, meaning the full bench of active judges refused to reconsider the three-judge panel’s decision.
“This result is frustrating, but my lawyers and I are looking at every possible option for what comes next,” McIver added.
The case stems from a heated oversight visit to a contentious immigration detention center in her state.

Last May, McIver arrived at the Delaney Hall detention center, a large Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) facility in New Jersey , for a congressional oversight visit. She arrived with two other members of Congress and Newark’s mayor, Ras Baraka.

McIver and the other officials were barred access into the detention center. While standing outside Delaney Hall, a federal agent attempted to arrest Baraka for refusing to depart the premises. According to a homeland security agent’s declaration , McIver intervened, attempting to prevent Baraka from being arrested.
Federal officials claim that during the pandemonium, McIver “slammed her forearm” into the homeland security agent and “forcibly” struck another deportation officer with her forearms.

“I hope that everyone who feels that way will stand with me in my fight against these unjust charges, because while I am the first lawmaker they have tried to jail, I will surely not be the last,” McIver said.

The court’s decision came a day after McIver got into a heated exchange with the homeland security secretary, Markwayne Mullin, for leading the agencies in charge of the Trump administration’s aggressive immigration crackdown.

The Delaney Hall facility has fallen under repeated scrutiny since it began detaining immigrants arrested by ICE again in 2025. At least three people detained at Delaney Hall have died. And the facility was the site of major clashes with ICE earlier this year during protests outside the facility in support of a hunger strike by detained immigrants.
McIver brought up conditions inside Delaney Hall and the number of who have died in ICE custody during Wednesday’s House committee hearing with Mullin.

“As you know, I am facing 17 years in prison, from this Trump administration, for my work at Delaney,” McIver said on Wednesday, then asked Mullin: “Do you even understand why I have been sounding the alarm about Delaney for so long?”
body_zh: 上诉法院驳回民主党拉莫尼卡·麦克莱弗 (LaMonica McIver) 针对 ICE 抗议提出的撤销指控的请求 | ICE（美国移民和海关执法局）
新泽西州女议员被控干涉移民逮捕，将因 2025 年 5 月事件接受审判
上诉法院周四裁定，新泽西州民主党众议员拉莫尼卡·麦克莱弗将继续面临与去年移民拘留中心外发生小规模冲突有关的指控，当时她试图在那里进行监督访问。
就在她就特朗普政府激进的移民执法行动向国土安全部长施压并告诉国土安全部长“你在杀人”的一天后，法院决定拒绝麦基弗推翻法院先前裁决的请求。
现在，根据法院的判决，她可能面临 2025 年 5 月事件的审判。
数据显示，ICE 为运营驱逐航班的承包商提供意外之财和保密
麦基弗在周四的一份声明中表示：“由于司法部武器化，也因为我敢于履行职责并监督 ICE，我将面临 17 年监禁。” “现在，由于第三巡回法庭令人失望的决定，我们都离这样一个世界又近了一步：美国总统可以仅仅因为不喜欢人们所代表的东西就试图监禁他们。”
麦基弗去年被指控袭击、抵抗、阻碍和干扰联邦官员。起诉引发了一场漫长的法律斗争，麦克莱弗声称起诉代表了特朗普政府的政治攻击。
麦基弗试图以各种理由驳回此案，包括辩称宪法保护她免受起诉。第三巡回上诉法院在八月份驳回了她的论点，并于周四拒绝了她举行“全席”听证会的请求，这意味着现任法官的全体法官拒绝重新考虑三名法官小组的决定。
麦克莱弗补充道：“这个结果令人沮丧，但我和我的律师正在考虑接下来发生的一切可能的选择。”
该案件源于对她所在州一个有争议的移民拘留中心的激烈监督访问。
去年五月，麦基弗抵达德莱尼霍尔拘留中心，这是新泽西州的一个大型移民和海关执法局 (ICE) 设施，进行国会监督访问。她与另外两名国会议员和纽瓦克市市长拉斯巴拉卡一起抵达。
麦克莱弗和其他官员被禁止进入拘留中心。当巴拉卡站在德莱尼厅外时，一名联邦特工试图逮捕拒绝离开该厅的巴拉卡。根据国土安全部特工的声明，麦克莱弗进行了干预，试图阻止巴拉卡被捕。
联邦官员声称，在混乱期间，麦基弗“用前臂猛击”国土安全人员，并用前臂“强行”击打另一名驱逐官员。
麦基弗说：“我希望每个有这种感觉的人都会与我站在一起，反对这些不公正的指控，因为虽然我是他们试图入狱的第一个立法者，但我肯定不会是最后一个。”
法院做出这一裁决的前一天，麦克莱弗与国土安全部长马克韦恩·穆林（Markwayne Mullin）因领导负责特朗普政府激进移民镇压的机构而发生激烈争执。
德莱尼厅设施自 2025 年再次开始拘留被 ICE 逮捕的移民以来，一直受到反复审查。德莱尼厅拘留所至少有三人死亡。今年早些时候，在该设施外举行支持被拘留移民绝食抗议的抗议活动时，该设施与 ICE 发生了重大冲突。
周三，在众议院委员会与穆林举行的听证会上，麦克莱弗提出了德莱尼厅内的情况以及在 ICE 拘留期间死亡的人数。
“如你所知，我将因在德莱尼的工作而面临特朗普政府 17 年的监禁，”麦基弗周三说道，然后问穆林：“你明白为什么我这么长时间以来一直对德莱尼发出警报吗？”

title_en: Leader of Democratic AG group to step down after Texas triumph
title_zh: 德克萨斯州获胜后民主党AG集团领导人辞职
summary: Sean Rankin led DAGA for a decade, helping Democrats flip five GOP-held attorney general offices.
summary_zh: 肖恩·兰金 (Sean Rankin) 领导 DAGA 十年，帮助民主党推翻了共和党控制的五个总检察长职位。
body_en: CHICAGO — The head of the Democratic Attorneys General Association is stepping down after a successful 2026 cycle in which their party flipped Republican-held attorney general offices in five states, including the conservative legal powerhouse of Texas.

Sean Rankin started as executive director at the group — known as DAGA — in 2016, and oversaw its operations as Democratic attorneys general banded together to challenge the first Trump administration over a range of issues. He became president of the group in 2022 and is credited with raising nearly $250 million for DAGA and its affiliated entities over the past decade.
“Since Sean joined DAGA in 2016, the committee has won the majority of their competitive races” against Republicans, “reshaping the map for Democrats,” the group said Thursday.
Rankin will stay at DAGA as it conducts a search for his successor.
Democrats will take control of at least five additional attorney general offices in January, following wins in Texas, Georgia, Ohio, Kansas and Iowa.
Alaska, which just elected a Democratic governor, is also expected to have a Democratic attorney general, since the governor appoints the state's top lawyer.

“On Texas, we took the head of the snake. So fundamentally, there will be a change in how the Republican attorneys general have to engage nationally if they do not have Texas at the front,” Rankin told POLITICO in a wide-ranging interview after the midterms earlier this month. “Texas has played an outsized role in the actions taken, in my opinion, against many of the issues that I care about, that the AGs fight for, that we believe the American people support — having Texas not on the other side, that’s a game changer.”
body_zh: 芝加哥——民主党总检察长协会主席即将辞职，此前民主党总检察长协会在 2026 年周期中取得了成功，该党在五个州推翻了共和党控制的总检察长职位，其中包括保守派法律强国德克萨斯州。
肖恩·兰金 (Sean Rankin) 于 2016 年开始担任该组织（称为 DAGA）的执行董事，并在民主党总检察长联合起来在一系列问题上挑战特朗普第一届政府时监督其运作。他于 2022 年成为该集团总裁，并在过去十年中为 DAGA 及其附属实体筹集了近 2.5 亿美元。
该组织周四表示，“自 2016 年肖恩加入 DAGA 以来，该委员会在与共和党的竞争中赢得了大部分”，“重塑了民主党的版图”。
兰金将留在 DAGA 寻找他的继任者。
继得克萨斯州、佐治亚州、俄亥俄州、堪萨斯州和爱荷华州获胜后，民主党将在一月份额外控制至少五个总检察长办公室。
刚刚选出民主党州长的阿拉斯加预计也将有一位民主党总检察长，因为州长任命了该州的首席律师。
“在德克萨斯州，我们拿下了蛇头。因此，从根本上来说，如果共和党总检察长没有德克萨斯州站在前线，他们在全国范围内的参与方式将会发生变化，”兰金在本月早些时候的中期选举后接受《政治》杂志采访时表示。 “在我看来，针对我关心的、AG 们为之奋斗的、我们相信美国人民支持的许多问题所采取的行动中，德克萨斯州发挥了巨大的作用——德克萨斯州不在另一边，这将改变游戏规则。”

title_en: Suspects charged in California train heist ring that netted cargo worth $22m
title_zh: 加州火车抢劫团伙犯罪嫌疑人被指控，该团伙盗窃了价值 2200 万美元的货物
summary: More than a dozen people allegedly targeted trains carrying Nike sneakers, Crocs footwear and other goods More than a dozen people were charged on Thursday with allegedly orchestrating a vast train heist operation to steal more than $22m in cargo – from popula
summary_zh: 据称，十几人袭击了载有耐克运动鞋、卡骆驰鞋和其他商品的火车 周四，十几人被指控
body_en: More than a dozen people allegedly targeted trains carrying Nike sneakers, Crocs footwear and other goods

More than a dozen people were charged on Thursday with allegedly orchestrating a vast train heist operation to steal more than $22m in cargo – from popular shoes to power tools – from major retailers .

A federal indictment unsealed on Thursday paints a picture of an organized group that targeted more than three dozen trains carrying Nike sneakers, Crocs footwear, power tools and other consumer goods that were imported into the United States through Los Angeles and Long Beach, which are home to the busiest ports in the country.

Trains that shuttle goods to stores and customers around the country have become a prominent target for large-scale theft in recent years, especially at large ports in the US that receive hundreds of millions of dollars of shipments every day. The relatively low-tech robberies have demanded attention from the world’s largest retailers, including the likes of Amazon .

The men would disable the trains at a planned location by busting the brakes, the indictment alleged, at which point the goods would be offloaded on to trucks. The goods were then peddled to an unnamed company that would resell the stolen merchandise for profit.
“The scale of the theft is staggering,” said first assistant United States attorney Bill Essayli, promising to prosecute any future efforts to steal the merchandise.

In group chats, the men shared numerous photos and videos of themselves busting into the hulking train cars, and posing with wads of cash and stolen merchandise. They also shared AI photos of themselves captioned “Los Trenes”, which means the trains in Spanish, beneath glamorized photos of men throwing boxes of shoes off trains into nearby cars while police helicopters descended overhead.
The 13 men were indicted for conspiracy and theft of interstate railroad cargo. Two were also charged with violence against railroad carriers.
If convicted, the men could face anywhere from five to 20 years in federal prison.
body_zh: 据称有十几人袭击了载有耐克运动鞋、卡骆驰鞋和其他商品的火车
周四，十多人被指控策划一场大规模火车抢劫行动，从主要零售商处窃取价值超过 2200 万美元的货物，从流行的鞋子到电动工具。
周四公布的一份联邦起诉书描绘了一个有组织的团伙针对三打多列载有耐克运动鞋、卡骆驰鞋类、电动工具和其他消费品的火车的画面，这些商品通过洛杉矶和长滩（美国最繁忙的港口所在地）进口到美国。
近年来，将货物运送到全国各地商店和顾客的火车已成为大规模盗窃的突出目标，特别是在每天接收数亿美元货物的美国大型港口。这些技术含量相对较低的抢劫案引起了全球最大零售商的关注，其中包括亚马逊等公司。
起诉书称，这些人会在计划地点通过踩刹车来使火车瘫痪，此时货物将被卸到卡车上。这些货物随后被兜售给一家未透露姓名的公司，该公司将被盗的商品转售以获取利润。
美国首席检察官比尔·埃赛利 (Bill Essayli) 表示，“盗窃的规模令人震惊”，他承诺将起诉未来任何盗窃商品的行为。
在群聊中，这些人分享了许多自己冲进笨重的火车车厢，并与大量现金和偷来的商品合影的照片和视频。他们还分享了自己的人工智能照片，标题为“Los Trenes”（西班牙语的意思是火车），照片下有男子将火车上的鞋子盒扔进附近的汽车，而警用直升机则从头顶降落。
这 13 名男子被指控串谋和盗窃州际铁路货物。其中两人还被指控对铁路承运人实施暴力。
如果罪名成立，这些人可能面临 5 至 20 年的联邦监狱监禁。

title_en: Appeals court grants Trump request to halt order restoring Venezuelan TPS
title_zh: 上诉法院批准特朗普停止恢复委内瑞拉 TPS 的命令的请求
summary: A federal appeals court in California has granted a request by the Trump administration to halt an order that would have restored deportation protections for Venezuelan migrants
summary_zh: 加利福尼亚州联邦上诉法院已批准特朗普政府的请求，暂停一项本可恢复驱逐出境保护的命令。
body_en: A federal appeals court in California has granted a request by the Trump administration to halt an order that would have restored deportation protections for Venezuelan migrants
By GISELA SALOMON Associated Press and LINDSAY WHITEHURST Associated Press

A federal appeals court has agreed to keep deportation protections frozen for hundreds of thousands of Venezuelan migrants, shortly after the Trump administration filed an emergency appeal to the Supreme Court.

The order handed down late Wednesday means the administration remains free to detain and deport Venezuelans who had previously been granted temporary protected status. Federal attorneys have said some 1,800 are in detention, and about 330 are subject to deportation proceedings.
The Supreme Court previously intervened to allow the administration to temporarily end the program for Venezuelans.
Congress created the TPS program in 1990 to protect migrants from deportation to countries experiencing natural disasters or civil unrest. The designation is granted in periods of up to 18 months.
The Trump administration argues that TPS is a temporary program and that Venezuela no longer meets the requirements for its renewal.

During President Donald Trump’s second term, the Department of Homeland Security has terminated TPS for more than 1 million people from 13 countries, including Venezuela, Haiti, Honduras, Nicaragua, Afghanistan and Syria.
However, in a shift in policy in recent months, the administration has maintained protections for nearly 200,000 Salvadorans and more than 100,000 people from Ukraine and Sudan.

TPS was first granted to Venezuelans in March 2021, under Democratic President Joe Biden. The designation was expanded in September 2023 to cover additional beneficiaries. About 600,000 Venezuelans have received TPS protections.

The Trump administration's move to end protections for Venezuelans was challenged in court, and a California-based judge ruled it unlawful. The Supreme Court twice intervened with temporary emergency orders, and later sent the case back to an appeals court after upholding the end of TPS for Haitians in a different case.

The U.S. 9th Circuit Court of Appeals had yet to rule when the administration returned to the Supreme Court on Wednesday, arguing that a temporary pause would soon expire and allow the restoration of deportation protections. Hours later, the appeals court extended its temporary freeze on protections until seven days after it hands down a full ruling.

After the Trump administration terminated TPS for Venezuelans last year, their work authorizations also became invalid. Thousands faced deportation proceedings, detention and removal. Many others chose to leave the country voluntarily.
It remains unclear how many Venezuelans who previously held TPS are still living in the United States.
body_zh: 加利福尼亚州联邦上诉法院已批准特朗普政府的请求，停止一项旨在恢复对委内瑞拉移民的驱逐保护的命令
吉塞拉·萨洛蒙 (GISELA SALOMON) 美联社和林赛·怀特赫斯特 (LINDSAY WHITEHURST) 美联社报道
在特朗普政府向最高法院提出紧急上诉后不久，联邦上诉法院同意继续冻结对数十万委内瑞拉移民的驱逐保护。
周三晚间下达的命令意味着政府仍然可以自由拘留和驱逐之前获得临时保护身份的委内瑞拉人。联邦检察官表示，约有 1,800 人被拘留，约 330 人面临驱逐出境程序。
最高法院此前进行干预，允许政府暂时终止针对委内瑞拉人的计划。
国会于 1990 年制定了 TPS 计划，旨在保护移民不被驱逐到遭受自然灾害或内乱的国家。该指定的授予期限最长为 18 个月。
特朗普政府辩称，TPS 是一项临时计划，委内瑞拉不再符合续签要求。
在唐纳德·特朗普总统的第二个任期内，国土安全部终止了来自委内瑞拉、海地、洪都拉斯、尼加拉瓜、阿富汗和叙利亚等 13 个国家的超过 100 万人的 TPS。
然而，近几个月来政策发生转变，政府继续对近 20 万萨尔瓦多人以及超过 10 万乌克兰和苏丹人提供保护。

TPS 于 2021 年 3 月在民主党总统乔·拜登的领导下首次授予委内瑞拉人。该指定于 2023 年 9 月扩大，以涵盖更多受益人。大约 60 万委内瑞拉人已获得 TPS 保护。
特朗普政府终止对委内瑞拉人保护的举措在法庭上受到质疑，加利福尼亚州的一名法官裁定其非法。最高法院两次以临时紧急令进行干预，并在另一起案件中维持终止对海地人的 TPS 后，将案件发回上诉法院。
当政府周三返回最高法院时，美国第九巡回上诉法院尚未做出裁决，称临时暂停很快就会到期，并允许恢复驱逐保护。几小时后，上诉法院将临时冻结保护期限延长至做出全面裁决后 7 天。
去年特朗普政府终止对委内瑞拉人的TPS后，他们的工作许可也随之失效。数千人面临驱逐程序、拘留和驱逐。还有许多人选择自愿离开该国。
目前尚不清楚有多少先前持有 TPS 的委内瑞拉人仍居住在美国。

summary_zh: 周四，特朗普总统乘坐空军一号从中国返回途中，召集特使史蒂夫·威特科夫和贾里德·库什纳举行会议。
body_en: On his way back from China Thursday aboard Air Force One, President Trump called in to a meeting his envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner were holding in Berlin with a group of European leaders and Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky.
"Putin wants to end the war, he wants the deal done, he is getting tired of this," Trump said, according to people in the room.

Why it matters: Instead of turning his historic trilateral summit with Chinese President Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin into a modern-day Yalta Conference, as some European and Ukrainian officials feared , Trump tried to use it to propel his push for peace in Europe.

Driving the news: Trump met Putin Thursday on the sidelines of the summit in Shenzhen. Their meeting wasn't originally on the schedule, but Trump wanted to discuss diplomatic efforts to end the war in Ukraine directly with the Russian president, a U.S. official said.
"Who is he? He's my friend," Trump said when he entered the meeting room where Putin was waiting.

Later in the day, Witkoff and Kushner told European leaders in Berlin that Trump pressed Putin to move on the peace talks, telling the Russian leader that now is the time to get a deal, according to a European official.
Trump also asked Xi for his help in ending the war during their bilateral meeting.

"He sent a very strong message to both of them [Putin and Xi] on the desire for peace, and would like to engage both of them very aggressively to get there," Kushner said at a press conference on Thursday.

Behind the scenes: As Trump wrapped up his meetings in China and headed back to Washington, his envoys started their talks with German Chancellor Friedrich Merz, French President Emmanuel Macron, British Prime Minister Andy Burnham, Zelensky and other European leaders.
Kushner and Witkoff tried to reassure the group that Trump doesn't intend to cut a deal with Putin over their heads.
"President Trump wants to make a deal with Europe by his side. He's not looking to impose anything unilaterally," Kushner said.
Shortly after, when Trump called in to brief the European leaders, he urged them to engage directly with Putin.
"Friedrich, you can make a call to Putin and this will make a deal," Trump said, referring to the German host.
Trump added, "Xi respects Zelensky. Putin is ready to do the deal. Zelensky can do a great deal."
What they're saying: A European official said the talks in Berlin were substantive, unlike the summit in Shenzhen, which was mostly symbolic.
"We think we have good coordination between the U.S. and Europe," the European official said.

State of play: One of the key U.S. objectives at the moment is to get Europe directly involved in peace talks between Russia and Ukraine. At the same time, U.S. officials also want Europe to engage in talks with Russia on a new European-Russian security agreement .
Putin said publicly for the first time Thursday that he is open to allowing the Europeans to participate in peace talks with Ukraine.

"We understand that it is pointless to discuss security issues, including those in Europe, without them," he said at a press conference after meeting with Trump. Putin added that Russia needs to understand what the Europeans are prepared to bring to the negotiations.
Putin also signaled willingness to present an updated proposal for a security agreement with Europe. "Life changes, so it makes no sense to return to geopolitical realities of the 1990s," he said.
body_zh: 周四，特朗普总统乘坐空军一号从中国返回途中，他的特使史蒂夫·威特科夫和贾里德·库什纳在柏林与欧洲领导人和乌克兰总统泽连斯基举行了会议。
据房间内的人士透露，特朗普说：“普京想要结束战争，他想要达成协议，他已经厌倦了。”
重要性：特朗普并没有像一些欧洲和乌克兰官员担心的那样，将与中国国家主席习近平和俄罗斯总统普京的历史性三边峰会变成现代的雅尔塔会议，而是试图利用它来推动欧洲和平。
推动这一消息的是：特朗普周四在深圳峰会期间会见了普京。一名美国官员表示，他们的会面原本并未列入日程，但特朗普希望直接与俄罗斯总统讨论结束乌克兰战争的外交努力。
“他是谁？他是我的朋友，”特朗普在走进普京正在等候的会议室时说道。
一位欧洲官员称，当天晚些时候，威特科夫和库什纳在柏林告诉欧洲领导人，特朗普敦促普京推进和谈，并告诉俄罗斯领导人现在是达成协议的时候了。
特朗普还在双边会晤期间请求习近平帮助结束战争。
库什纳在周四的新闻发布会上表示：“他向普京和习近平发出了非常强烈的信息，表达了对和平的渴望，并希望与他们积极接触以实现这一目标。”
幕后花絮：当特朗普结束在中国的会议并返回华盛顿时，他的特使开始与德国总理弗里德里希·梅尔茨、法国总统埃马纽埃尔·马克龙、英国首相安迪·伯纳姆、泽连斯基和其他欧洲领导人举行会谈。
库什纳和威特科夫试图向该组织保证，特朗普不打算在他们的领导下与普京达成协议。
“特朗普总统希望与欧洲达成协议。他不打算单方面强加任何东西，”库什纳说。
不久之后，当特朗普打电话向欧洲领导人通报情况时，他敦促他们直接与普京接触。
“弗里德里希，你可以给普京打电话，这样就能达成协议，”特朗普指的是德国东道主。
特朗普补充道，“习近平尊重泽连斯基。普京已准备好达成协议。泽连斯基可以做很多事情。”
他们的说法：一位欧洲官员表示，柏林峰会具有实质性内容，与深圳峰会不同，后者主要是象征性的。
“我们认为美国和欧洲之间有着良好的协调，”这位欧洲官员表示。
现状：美国目前的主要目标之一是让欧洲直接参与俄罗斯和乌克兰之间的和谈。与此同时，美国官员还希望欧洲与俄罗斯就新的欧俄安全协议进行谈判。
普京周四首次公开表示，他对允许欧洲参与与乌克兰的和平谈判持开放态度。
他在与特朗普会面后的新闻发布会上表示：“我们明白，在没有安全问题的情况下讨论包括欧洲在内的安全问题是毫无意义的。”普京补充说，俄罗斯需要了解欧洲人准备为谈判带来什么。
普京还表示愿意提出与欧洲达成安全协议的最新提案。 “生活发生了变化，因此回到 20 世纪 90 年代的地缘政治现实是没有意义的，”他说。
